adelboden.note: Through the Engstligen valley from Frutigen to the resort below the Engstligenalp, steady with a few hairpins at the end. Open all year.

alagna-valsesia.note: The long valley road of the Valsesia from Varallo to its end at Alagna, a Walser village below the east face of Monte Rosa. Gentle, open all year.

albulapass.note: Closure usually early November. Quiet road alongside the Rhaetian Railway.

alpe-d-huez.note: Road to a ski resort, open all year. Scenically rather plain, but pure legend.

alpe-di-neggia.note: 1,200 m up from Lake Maggiore on the Gambarogno shore, in hairpins through chestnut forest with the lake below; beyond the summit the road drops to Indemini, which is connected to the road network only from the Italian side. Usually snow at the top from December to April.

altopiano-del-cansiglio.classicAscent: 21.4 km, 4.1 % from Vittorio Veneto to Pian Cansiglio
altopiano-del-cansiglio.note: The beech forest of the Venetian fleet, today a quiet plateau with karst meadows and mist-filled lakes. The ascent from Vittorio Veneto is even, and there is almost nothing going on at the top.

altopiano-di-asiago.classicAscent: 33.8 km, 2.6 % from Bassano del Grappa to Asiago
altopiano-di-asiago.note: The plateau of the Seven Communes, wide and flat at the top, traces of the mountain war everywhere along its edges. The ascent drags on; the loops on top are the real destination; cleared all year.

arcalis.note: The climb to the end of the Valira del Nord valley at the Ordino-Arcalís resort, a Tour finish several times; wide hairpins at the top. Cleared all year.

arlbergpass.note: Open all year, traffic despite the tunnel.

arolla.note: Up the whole Val d'Hérens, past the earth pyramids of Euseigne and through Evolène; from Les Haudères it turns steep and climbs in hairpins to the foot of Mont Collon. Long rather than steep, open to the village all year.

arosa.note: Up the Schanfigg from Chur to the dead end at Arosa, a winding road high above the Plessur. Steady, open all year; the way back is the same road.

avoriaz.note: The road from Morzine to the car-free ski resort on the rock edge above the valley, a Tour de France stage finish several times. Steady at around 7 %, cleared all year.

axalp.note: From Brienz steeply via Giessbach up to the alp above the Brienzersee, almost 1,000 m of climbing with a view of the lake. Open all year.

ballon-d-alsace.note: In 1905 the very first climb of the Tour de France. Three ascents on a wide road, the shortest and steepest from Saint-Maurice-sur-Moselle; at the top pastures, inns and weekend day-trippers.

ballon-de-servance.note: A quiet, narrow forest road (D16) from Plancher-les-Mines over the shoulder of the Ballon de Servance to the Col des Croix and down to Le Thillot, the opening climb of Les 3 Ballons. Few views, only a car park in the woods at the top; the surface towards Le Thillot is bumpy in places.

barrage-d-emosson.classicAscent: 13 km, 6 % from Le Châtelard via Finhaut
barrage-d-emosson.note: From Le Châtelard via Finhaut to the dam, at the top a reservoir with the Mont Blanc massif behind it; a Tour de France finish in 2016. Narrow and steep above Finhaut, closed in winter.

barrage-de-la-grande-dixence.note: From Sion via Vex and Hérémence into the Val des Dix to the foot of the world's tallest gravity dam – more than 1,600 m of climbing in long, even ramps. The top section is closed in winter, and the way back is the same road.

berninapass.note: Open all year, glacier views at Lago Bianco.

bielmonte.note: The Panoramica Zegna from Trivero along the ridge of the Biellese Alps to Bielmonte, in early summer between flowering rhododendrons, with a view of Monte Rosa. Long and moderate.

bocca-del-creer.note: The road over Monte Baldo: from Brentonico via San Valentino onto the ridge to the Bocca del Creer, then over the Bocca di Navene 1,500 m almost vertically above Lake Garda down to Navene. The lake side is narrow, steep and the finest descent on the lake; closed in winter.

boedele.note: Dornbirn's own mountain and the shortest link into the Bregenzerwald: steeply up through forest from Dornbirn, on the other side a short drop to Schwarzenberg. Open all year.

bosco-gurin.note: From the Maggia valley up through the Val di Campo to the highest village in Ticino, a Walser settlement. Steadily steep, open all year.

brennerpass.note: The crossing from the Wipptal into the Eisack valley; cyclists ride the old Brenner road (B 182, SS 12) beside the motorway and the railway. Open all year, long and flat from Innsbruck, shorter from Sterzing with one steeper stretch at Gossensass; the second climb of the Ötztaler Radmarathon, with heavy traffic on the main road.

breuil-cervinia.note: Through the Valtournenche to the foot of the Matterhorn, long and even, a Giro d'Italia finish most recently in 2018. Open all year, with a lot of day-trip traffic at weekends.

bruenigpass.note: The main road from Lucerne into the Bernese Oberland, wide and heavily used. Short on both sides, open all year; unavoidable as the link to the Grimsel and the Susten.

campo-carlo-magno.note: The crossing between Val Rendena and Val di Sole, directly above Madonna di Campiglio, with the Brenta on one side and the Adamello on the other. Cleared all year as a ski resort and busy in winter and summer alike.

capanna-dotra.classicAscent: 6.0 km, 7 % from the junction on the Lukmanier road
capanna-dotra.note: A detour off the Lukmanier's south side: a narrow road climbs to the Capanna Dötra at just over 1700 m. Season window taken from the Lukmanierpass.

cari.note: From Faido in many hairpins up to the sunny terrace above the Leventina, steadily steep and hardly used. Open all year.

ceillac-vallee-du-melezet.classicAscent: 13.5 km, 7 % from the junction at the Maison du Roy
ceillac-vallee-du-melezet.note: A detour off the Izoard climb from Guillestre: at the Maison du Roy the road to Ceillac branches off and ends at the head of the Vallée du Mélézet. Season window taken from the Col d'Izoard.
ascents: Junction at the Maison du Roy

chaillol.note: The road from Saint-Bonnet up to the small Chaillol resort, quiet and steady, at the top the view over the Champsaur. Cleared all year.

chamrousse.note: Grenoble's home climb: from Uriage-les-Bains through forest to over 1,700 m at the ski resort, a Tour de France finish in 2014. Cleared all year.

chasseral.note: The saddle below the highest summit of the Bernese Jura, at the top the view over three lakes to the Alps. Closed in winter.

cima-grappa.note: The solitary peak above the Venetian plain: over 1,500 m of climbing in one go from every side, at the top the First World War ossuary and the view from the Adriatic to the Dolomites. The road from Semonzo is the Strada Cadorna, narrow and without shade in its upper part.

cinque-torri.classicAscent: 4.2 km, 10 % from the junction on the Falzarego road
cinque-torri.note: A detour off the Falzarego climb from Cortina: a steep dead-end road up to the Rifugio Cinque Torri below the five rock towers. A ski area in winter, when the road cannot be ridden.

cipressa.classicAscent: 5.6 km, 4 % from San Lorenzo al Mare
cipressa.note: A village hill above the coast and the climb where Milan–Sanremo has come apart since 1982. Up from the Aurelia into the village, olives at the top, then the descent to Santo Stefano al Mare. Open all year; famous it is, hard it is not.

cirque-du-fer-a-cheval.classicAscent: 6.2 km, 3.2 % from Sixt-Fer-à-Cheval to the head of the valley
cirque-du-fer-a-cheval.note: Six flat kilometres into a valley head ringed by waterfalls in a semicircle of 700-metre walls. Short, easy and still one of the great sights of the Northern Alps.

cogne.note: Through the narrow gorge of the Grand Eyvia into the Val di Cogne, to the edge of the Gran Paradiso national park; between rock walls at the bottom, on the meadows of Sant'Orso at the top. Steady and open all year.

col-d-agnes.note: The wild pass of the Couserans across wide pastures, a double crossing with the Port de Lers beyond. Steep from Aulus, long from Massat. Closed in winter.

col-d-allos.note: Closure usually from November. Together with the Cayolle and the Champs, the 'triple loop' from Barcelonnette.

col-d-aspin.note: The pass between Arreau and the Campan valley, at the top open pastures with cows and horses and the view of the Pic du Midi. A classic Tour pass, closed in winter.

col-d-aubisque.note: A Tour pass since 1910: from Laruns via Eaux-Bonnes and Gourette steeply up, to the east the balcony road of the Cirque du Litor to the Soulor. Closed above Gourette in winter.

col-d-azet.note: The crossing from the Aure valley into the Louron valley, steep on both sides and with a wide view; often in the Tour route between the Peyresourde and Saint-Lary. Closed at times after snowfall.

col-d-ey.note: The home climb of Buis-les-Baronnies, short and even between olive groves and apricots, the view of the Ventoux at the top. Open all year; the opener of every Baronnies loop.

col-d-eze.note: The mountain time trial of Paris–Nice, for decades the closing act of the race: from Nice over the Grande Corniche with the sea below to the col, La Turbie and Monaco beyond. Open all year, busy; the east side from Èze is under two kilometres and no ascent in its own right.

col-d-ispeguy.note: The small border pass from the Baïgorry valley into the Baztan, across green pastures with a view over the Basque country. Open all year.

col-d-izoard.note: Casse Déserte on the south side. Closure usually early November; October is generally fine, with an eye on the weather.

col-d-oderen.note: A gentle crossing from the upper Thur valley to Ventron in the Moselotte valley, quiet and wooded.

col-d-ornon.note: Open all year, even and quiet – the relaxed link from the Oisans into the Valbonnais.

col-de-bagargui.note: The crossing in the Basque country between Larrau and the Iraty forest, wide pastures with horses and sheep at the top. Narrow, closed in winter.

col-de-bleine.note: The highest crossing between the Estéron and the Thorenc plateau; hairpins through beech forest on the north side, meadows and limestone ridges at the top. Open all year, briefly closed after snowfall.

col-de-bramont.note: A quiet crossing from La Bresse into the uppermost Thur valley at Wildenstein, short and steady.

col-de-braus.note: Open all year, a classic winter training destination for the pros on the Côte d'Azur. The ladder of hairpins above L'Escarène is famous enough to have its own photos.

col-de-brouis.note: From Sospel into the Roya valley to Breil: the crossing that links Sospel with Tende and the railway line. Open all year; from Breil the longer side.

col-de-bussang.note: The N66 from Thann to Remiremont: heavy traffic and lorries, flat enough to link two rides, not a goal in itself. The source of the Moselle is at the top.

col-de-castillon.note: The direct way from Menton to Sospel, open all year: from the sea through the Careï gorge and via the rebuilt village of Castillon to the pass, down into the Bévéra valley. Traffic on the Menton side.

col-de-champex.note: The resort on its mountain lake above the Val d'Entremont, a quiet parallel to the Great St Bernard road between Les Valettes and Orsières. From Orsières steady in hairpins, from Les Valettes narrow, winding and clearly steeper; as a ski resort reachable all year.

col-de-chateauneuf.note: The first mountain behind Nice towards Tourrette-Levens and Contes, the opener of many training loops out of the city; with traffic, open all year.

col-de-fontaube.note: From Buis via Eygaliers onto the ridge and down into the Toulourenc valley beneath the north face of the Ventoux; the road continues to Brantes and Montbrun. Open all year and almost without traffic.

col-de-grosse-pierre.note: A short wooded crossing between Gérardmer and the Moselotte valley at Cornimont.

col-de-jau.note: The quiet crossing from the Conflent into the upper Aude valley, steady from Mosset, long through gorges from Axat. Closed in winter.

col-de-joux.note: From the spa town of Saint-Vincent in many hairpins through chestnut and larch forest into the Val d'Ayas, on the other side a short drop to Brusson. Open all year; with the valley road down to Verrès it makes a loop.

col-de-joux-plane.note: Closure usually from December. Short, steep, Mont Blanc view at the end.

col-de-l-echelle.note: The low crossing from the Clarée valley to Bardonecchia; on the Italian side a steep wall of hairpins with short tunnels. Closed in winter.

col-de-l-homme-mort.note: The crossing from Montbrun onto the lavender plateau of Ferrassières and Sault, open all year; the west side from the plateau is hardly a climb, the east side a quiet forest road with a view of the Lure.

col-de-l-iseran.note: Highest road pass in the Alps. Often closed as early as early to mid-October, open from June.

col-de-l-orme.note: The first step from Lucéram up to Peïra-Cava and the Turini; a pass of its own only on paper, but the road on which the Nice loops over the Turini begin. Open all year.

col-de-la-bataille.note: The crossing from Léoncel through a short tunnel beneath the Rochers de la Sausse onto the balcony above the Combe de Bouvante; beyond the col the D199 is not cleared in winter and is closed between barriers. Only the Léoncel side is a climb; to the east the road runs on as a rolling balcony over the Col de la Portette to Lente.

col-de-la-biche.note: The saddle north of the Grand Colombier, over which the ridge road to the Colombier runs; narrow forest roads from the Valromey. Closed in winter.

col-de-la-bonette.note: Highest paved loop in Europe. Usually open until mid/late October, closure weather-dependent.

col-de-la-cayolle.note: Closure usually from November. Narrow, lonely, gorges and marmots.

col-de-la-core.note: The pass over the Bethmale valley between Seix and Castillon, at the top the view of the Mont Valier. Open all year, closed at times after snowfall.

col-de-la-couillole.note: Usually open all year, little traffic.

col-de-la-croix.note: Narrow, steep link from Villars to Les Diablerets, closed in winter. Alpine pastures at the top with a view of the Muveran; markedly quieter than the parallel way through the valley.

col-de-la-croix-de-fer.note: Closure usually early November. Irregular profile with counter-climbs.

col-de-la-croix-de-la-serra.note: The pass south of Saint-Claude into the Valserine valley, moderate through forest and across pastures. Open all year.

col-de-la-croix-fry.note: The crossing from Thônes through the Manigod valley to La Clusaz, the quiet sister of the Aravis road with a view of the Aravis range. Open all year, a small ski resort at the top.

col-de-la-faucille.note: The main crossing from Geneva into the Haut-Jura: from Gex in hairpins up the eastern flank, at the top the view over Lake Geneva to Mont Blanc. Cleared all year, with traffic.

col-de-la-forclaz-de-montmin.note: Open all year. The top hangs like a balcony above the Lac d'Annecy; the paragliding launch site is correspondingly busy on fine days.

col-de-la-forclaz-martigny.note: The way from Martigny to Chamonix, evenly steep through vineyards and then forest. Cleared all year and, as the main link into the Trient valley, busy accordingly; often ridden as the approach to the Col des Montets.

col-de-la-givrine.note: The long climb from Nyon on Lake Geneva via Saint-Cergue onto the Jura ridge and on into France. Steady, cleared all year.

col-de-la-lebe.note: The gentle crossing between the Valromey and Belley, through forest and across pastures. Open all year.

col-de-la-lombarde.note: Border pass into Piedmont. Closure usually mid/late October.

col-de-la-loze.note: The upper part is a car-free cycle path with ramps above 20 %. Usually rideable until late October.

col-de-la-madeleine.note: Closure usually early November. Long, evenly grinding ascent.

col-de-la-madeleine-bedoin.note: The little crossing between Malaucène and Bédoin that closes the Ventoux loop: short, with a view of the mountain and the Dentelles. Open all year. Not to be confused with the great Col de la Madeleine in Savoie.

col-de-la-madone.note: Open all year and almost free of traffic, because there is only a village at the top. Famous as a form test: anyone who is fast here is in form.

col-de-la-pierre-saint-martin.note: The westernmost high pass of the Pyrenees, a Tour finish in 2015: from Arette more than 1,400 m up into the karst landscape on the border. Cleared to the resort all year.

col-de-la-porte.note: Beyond Coaraze to the crossing to Lucéram, a little above the Col Saint-Roch: quiet, with a view of the villages of the Paillon. Open all year.

col-de-la-ramaz.note: Little traffic, with a gallery and a steep middle section around 10 %. Alpine pasture at the top rather than a ski resort.

col-de-la-schlucht.note: The main crossing from Colmar to Gérardmer, with the traffic to match, cleared in winter; on the Tour de France route in 2023. From Munster the finer and steeper side, from Gérardmer via Xonrupt almost flat; the Route des Crêtes starts at the top.

col-de-latrape.note: The gentle saddle between the Garbet valley and Aulus, often ridden as the approach to the Col d'Agnes. Open all year.

col-de-macuegne.note: Between Montbrun-les-Bains and Séderon, over lavender fields and beech forest with the Ventoux at your back. Open all year, quiet; the way back on the Perty loop.

col-de-manse.note: Gap's home climb and the crossing into the Champsaur, steady and moderate. Open all year.

col-de-marie-blanque.note: The crossing from the Vallée d'Aspe into the Ossau, from Escot with the last four kilometres at around 11 %, the Bénou plateau at the top. Open all year.

col-de-menee.note: The quiet crossing from the Diois into the Trièves on the southern edge of the Vercors, at the top a short summit tunnel at around 1,400 m and on the north side the view of the Mont Aiguille. Open all year.

col-de-mente.note: The steep pass between the Garonne valley and the Ger de Boutx, a classic chain with the Portet d'Aspet. Open all year, cleared to the resort at the top.

col-de-montgenevre.note: Border crossing into Italy, open all year and correspondingly busy. Unspectacular as a climb, practical as a link.

col-de-murs.note: From Venasque over the Monts de Vaucluse to the village of Murs and on to Gordes: limestone, oaks, lavender and hardly any traffic. Open all year; the link from the Ventoux country into the Luberon.

col-de-nice.note: The hill between the Paillon of L'Escarène and that of Contes; short, open all year, and with Braus and Saint-Roch the rest of the loop. From Contes the road comes over the Col de Châteauneuf, hence only the east side.

col-de-notre-dame-des-abeilles.note: The road from Bédoin to Sault through the forest on the south flank of the Ventoux, open all year; the second way to Sault besides the Nesque, even and without hairpins.

col-de-pailheres.note: The highest pass in the Ariège, crossed by the Tour several times: from Ax via Ascou long and steep, at the top a cascade of hairpins above the pastures. Closed in winter.

col-de-perty.note: One of the highest passes in the Baronnies, Tour de France passage in 2006: from the Ouvèze out of the forest into a wide bowl, at the top the view of the Ventoux and the Lure. Open all year, briefly not after snowfall.

col-de-peyresourde.note: The Tour classic between Luchon and the Louron valley, steadily steep from Luchon, long and gentler from Arreau. The Peyragudes resort beside the top. Cleared all year.

col-de-plainpalais.note: The way from Chambéry into the Bauges, past the Margériaz mountain to Le Châtelard. A real climb from Chambéry, a gentle valley crossing from the Bauges. Open all year.

col-de-port.note: The gentle crossing from Tarascon to Massat, long and steady through forest. Open all year.

col-de-puymorens.note: The pass between the upper Ariège valley and the Cerdagne; through traffic has used the tunnel since 1994, and the pass road is quieter. Cleared, closed at times after snowfall.

col-de-richemond.note: The crossing from the Rhône valley at Seyssel onto the Hotonnes plateau, long and gentle through forest. Open all year.

col-de-romme.note: Balcony road above the Arve valley, steep and narrow at the top. On the Tour's programme since 2009 as the starter before the Colombière.

col-de-saint-jean.note: A small Baronnies pass on the D170 between Laborel and Eygalayes, short, quiet and with a chapel at the top; often linked with the Perty and the Macuègne into a loop. Open all year, briefly not after snowfall.

col-de-sainte-marie.note: The old crossing from Sainte-Marie-aux-Mines into Lorraine; most of the through traffic now takes the Maurice-Lemaire tunnel below it.

col-de-sarenne.note: The quiet back side of Alpe d'Huez: narrow, rough and without any infrastructure. The surface on the east side is coarse in places.

col-de-soubeyrand.note: From Sainte-Jalle over the ridge into the Eygues valley at Curnier: hairpins through oaks and lavender, hardly a car. Open all year.

col-de-spandelles.note: A narrow, quiet mountain road between the Ouzom valley and the Argelès valley, better known since the 2022 Tour. Partly rough surface, closed in winter.

col-de-turini.note: Famous from the Monte Carlo Rally, open all year.

col-de-valberg.note: The crossing from the Var valley at Guillaumes to Beuil through the Valberg resort; with the Couillole and the Gorges du Cians a classic loop. Cleared all year.

col-de-vars.note: Closure usually late November. Classic combination with the Izoard or the Bonette.

col-de-vence.note: Open all year, karst plateau above the coast. The winter training ground of the pros around Nice.

col-des-annes.note: A dead-end road from Le Grand-Bornand via Le Chinaillon onto the alpine plateau below the Pointe Percée, at the top cheese farms and the view of Mont Blanc. Narrow and steep in its upper part; closed above Le Chinaillon in winter.

col-des-aravis.note: Open all year, on the Tour's programme since 1911. From the top the view of Mont Blanc; heavy traffic in summer.

col-des-champs.note: Very quiet, mediocre tarmac. Closure usually from November.

col-des-etroits.note: The road from the Yverdon plain via Sainte-Croix into the Val de Travers, lower down through the Covatanne gorge. Open all year.

col-des-gets.note: The crossing from the Giffre valley into the Dranse valley, part of the Route des Grandes Alpes, with the ski resort of Les Gets on the top. Cleared all year; the real climb comes from Taninges, from Morzine it is only a little over 4 km and 150 m of climbing. Busy on the D 902 in summer, lorries included.

col-des-montets.note: The low barrier between the Chamonix valley and Vallorcine, right beneath the Aiguilles Rouges. Short and never steep; closed at times in winter when there is avalanche danger.

col-des-mosses.note: The broad link from the Rhône valley into the Pays-d'Enhaut, with a high moor at the top instead of a summit. Cleared all year, even and without surprises.

col-des-saisies.note: Ski resort on the top, cleared all year. Wide, even road – the link between the Beaufortain and the Val d'Arly.

col-du-bonhomme.note: The crossing from Kaysersberg to Saint-Dié on the main road, with traffic. At the top the crest road heads south to the Col du Calvaire and the Schlucht.

col-du-calvaire.note: Above the Lac Blanc at the northern end of the crest road. Northwards the road stays on the crest to the Col du Bonhomme – not a second ascent.

col-du-chaussy.classicAscent: 13.8 km, 7.5 % from Pontamafrey via the Lacets de Montvernier
col-du-chaussy.note: The seventeen hairpins of the Lacets de Montvernier stack up on top of each other over two kilometres like a piece of architecture – a Tour regular since 2015. Above them the road turns quiet and narrow.

col-du-coq.note: The hardest pass of the Chartreuse: from the Grésivaudan at Saint-Ismier more than 1,000 m up the cliff flank, at the top the view of the Belledonne. Gentler towards Saint-Pierre-de-Chartreuse. Closed in winter.

col-du-corbier.note: A short, steep crossing in the Chablais between the Dranse valley and the Vallée d'Aulps, at the top pastures and a small ski lift. Open all year.

col-du-cucheron.note: The short crossing in the heart of the Chartreuse between Saint-Pierre-d'Entremont and Saint-Pierre-de-Chartreuse, the link between the Granier and the Porte. Open all year.

col-du-galibier.classicAscent: 18 km, 6.9 % from Valloire (34 km via Télégraphe)
col-du-galibier.note: Winter closure usually late October to early June. Early October is often still glorious; from mid-October there is a risk of snow at the top.

col-du-glandon.note: Closure usually early November. Ramps of up to 11 % just before the top.

col-du-grand-saint-bernard.note: Pass road (not the tunnel) usually closed from mid-October.

col-du-granier.note: The pass below the north face of the Mont Granier, the crossing from Chambéry into the Chartreuse. Long and moderate from Chambéry, shorter from Entremont. Open all year.

col-du-granon.note: Military road with no way through, nothing at the top but meadows and the view of the Écrins. Tour finish in 1986 and 2022; the gradient barely eases between 8 and 11 %.

col-du-hundsruck.note: A short wooded pass between Thann and the Doller valley at Masevaux, easy to combine with the Ballon d'Alsace.

col-du-lautaret.note: National road, cleared all year. Feeder to the Galibier, heavy traffic.

col-du-marchairuz.note: The highest road pass of the Swiss Jura, from the Lake Geneva basin at Bière into the Vallée de Joux; pastures and forest at the top. Often closed in winter after snowfall.

col-du-mollard.note: Eighteen hairpins through forest and hamlets, hardly any traffic; at the top the view opens onto the Aiguilles d'Arves.

col-du-mollendruz.note: The short crossing from the Vaud plateau into the Vallée de Joux at L'Abbaye. Moderate, cleared all year.

col-du-mont-cenis.note: Closure usually from November. High plateau with a reservoir.

col-du-noyer.note: The northern ramp clings in hairpins to the wall of the Dévoluy, and the top looks out over the whole Champsaur. Closed in winter.

col-du-petit-ballon.note: A bare dome with mountain inns and a view over the Munster valley and the Rhine plain, on the Tour de France route in 2023. Narrow and steep from Wasserbourg; the south side from the Florival via Linthal is still missing here, because no router takes it without a detour.

col-du-petit-saint-bernard.note: Border pass, closure usually late October/November.

col-du-pillon.note: Across from Les Diablerets to Gsteig, with the Diablerets glacier above the road. Short, cleared all year and usually joined with the Col de la Croix into a loop.

col-du-platzerwasel.note: Steep out of the upper Munster valley at Sondernach up to the crest. From the south the pass is reached via the Markstein at crest height – not a climb of its own.

col-du-portet.note: Beyond the Pla d'Adet to over 2,200 m, a Tour finish in 2018 and 2021. At the top a narrow strip of tarmac across the pastures with a view into the Néouvielle. Closed in winter.

col-du-portet-d-aspet.note: The pass between the Comminges and the Couserans; on the descent to the west a memorial recalls Fabio Casartelli, who died here in a crash during the 1995 Tour. Open all year.

col-du-portillon.note: The short border pass from Luchon into the Val d'Aran to Bossòst, steady through forest on both sides. Open all year.

col-du-pourtalet.note: The long border pass from the Ossau valley into Aragon, the Pic du Midi d'Ossau at the top. Moderate but long; a main road with lorries. Cleared all year, closed at times after snowfall.

col-du-pre.note: Steep, shaded ramps all the way to the top, then the Lac de Roselend from above – the finest way to reach the Cormet de Roselend.

col-du-rousset.note: Open all year, the road serves the ski station. The top is the southern portal of the tunnel; the actual saddle lies 170 m higher, above the bore. Beyond the tunnel the high plateau of the Vercors opens up.

col-du-sanetsch.note: From Sion over 1,700 m of climbing in one go up to the reservoir – the only way down is back along the same road, or by cable car to Gsteig. Several unlit tunnels, a treeless karst landscape at the top.

col-du-somport.note: The old border pass of the Vallée d'Aspe to Canfranc; since the tunnel the traffic goes underneath, and the pass road on top is quiet. Long and gentle.

col-du-soulor.note: The Aubisque's forerunner above the Val d'Azun, short and steady from Arrens, through the quiet Ouzom valley from Ferrières. Closed at times after snowfall.

col-du-telegraphe.note: Open all year, a forest road at a steady 7 %. A solid climb in its own right, but usually just the first step towards the Galibier.

col-du-tourmalet.note: The most-ridden pass of the Tour de France and the highest road pass of the French central Pyrenees: two sides of around 1,300 m each, the Géant statue at the top. From the east through the La Mongie ski resort. Closed above La Mongie and Barèges in winter.

col-du-wettstein.note: Between the Munster valley and Orbey, with a First World War military cemetery at the top and the Lingekopf battlefield next to it.

col-saint-martin.note: Approach to the small station of La Colmiane, cleared all year. Short, even, forest hairpins.

col-saint-roch.note: Between Lucéram and Coaraze, two mountain villages of the Paillon hinterland: quiet, open all year and the link that turns Braus and Turini into a loop.

coll-d-ordino.note: The quiet pass between Ordino and Canillo, away from the main road and with a view over the valleys of Andorra. Closed at times after snowfall.

collada-de-toses.note: The long crossing from the Ripollès into the Cerdanya, in wide hairpins via La Molina on the east side. A main road, cleared all year.

colle-d-esischie.note: The crossing from the Maira into the Grana valley, a good kilometre below the Colle Fauniera, which the road continues up to. Only the Maira side from Ponte Marmora is listed: from Pradleves it is the Fauniera ascent up to just short of its summit. Narrow, rough tarmac, closed like the Fauniera usually from mid-October.

colle-d-oggia.note: Up from Carpasio in the Argentina hinterland and down to Rezzo: the loop the Sanremo pros spend their winters on. Open all year, almost no cars.

colle-del-lys.note: The crossing from the lower Susa valley into the Valli di Lanzo, at the top a memorial to the partisans. Short and stiff from Rubiana, long and gentle from Viù. Open all year.

colle-del-melogno.note: The home climb of Finale Ligure: through the beech woods of the Melogno to 1,000 m, the fort of 1880 at the top and occasional snow in winter, otherwise open all year. From Calizzano the shorter, less busy side.

colle-del-nivolet.note: Dead end in the Gran Paradiso National Park, the top section car-free on summer weekends. Usually closed from October.

colle-dell-agnello.note: Border pass, usually closed from early/mid-October. Lonely and magnificent when it is open.

colle-della-maddalena.note: The crossing from the Valle Stura into the Ubaye valley, long and moderate, at the top the Lago della Maddalena and wide pastures. Cleared all year and therefore also a lorry route between Cuneo and Barcelonnette.

colle-delle-finestre.classicAscent: 18.5 km, 9.2 % from Susa, top 8 km gravel
colle-delle-finestre.note: Giro legend with a gravel finale. Usually open until late October, muddy after rain.

colle-di-nava.note: The crossing from the Riviera into the Tanaro valley, open all year and the road by which the Giro and the Milano–Torino classics reached Liguria. Long and even from Pieve di Teco, shorter from Ormea via Ponte di Nava; lavender fields at the top.

colle-di-zambla.note: The crossing between the Val Seriana and the Val Brembana via Oltre il Colle, with a view of the Pizzo Arera. Steady from Ponte Nossa, long via the Val Serina from Ambria. Open all year.

colle-fauniera.note: Pantani memorial at the top, rough tarmac. Closure usually from mid-October.

colle-gallo.note: Between the Val Seriana and the Val Cavallina; at the top the sanctuary with the Madonna dei Ciclisti, the counterpart to the Ghisallo. Giro passage in 2011 and a training route of the Bergamasque pros. Open all year.

colle-langan.note: Between the Nervia valley of Pigna and the Argentina valley of Molini di Triora, open all year. On the Pigna side long and lonely through forest, the view of Monte Toraggio at the top; the road that connects the two most beautiful valleys of the hinterland.

colle-melosa.classicAscent: 6.7 km, 7 % from the junction on the Langan road
colle-melosa.note: A detour off the Colle Langan: the road climbs to the refuge at the Colle Melosa. Not cleared in winter.

colle-san-bartolomeo.note: Links the Impero valley behind Imperia with the Arroscia valley of Pieve di Teco, open all year. A winter training climb for the pros of the Riviera: olive groves, hardly any traffic, a village at the top.

colle-san-bernardo-di-garessio.note: The old road from Albenga to Garessio in the Tanaro valley, open all year. Up from Erli on the Neva through chestnuts, short and steep down to Garessio on the north side; links the Riviera with the loops of Ormea and Nava.

colle-san-carlo.note: Aosta Valley, brutally steep, closure usually from November.

colle-scravaion.classicAscent: 13 km, 5 % from Castelvecchio di Rocca Barbena
colle-scravaion.note: The crossing behind Albenga to Bardineto and Calizzano, open all year. Evenly up via the castle village of Castelvecchio on the south side; the Melogno loop from Finale returns to the sea here.

combe-laval.note: Maintained all year, occasional closures for rockfall. The final kilometres hang as a gallery in the wall of the Cirque de Combe Laval, eleven tunnels included; at the top the road crosses the Col de la Machine into the high valley of Lente.

cormet-de-roselend.note: Closure usually early November. Reservoir scenery, one of the most beautiful roads in Savoy.

corniche-sublime.note: The south side of the Verdon, open all year. From the Balcons de la Mescla you look 300 m straight down; on summer weekends it is correspondingly busy.

crans-montana.note: From Sierre through vineyards and villages up to the sunny plateau with its lakes and golf course, steady and steep and open all year. A resort with traffic, but with the wide view across the Rhône valley to the Valais four-thousanders.

culmine-di-san-pietro.note: The crossing from the Valsassina into the Val Taleggio, Giro passage in 2008 and 2018; short and even from Moggio, from Vedeseta the longer, quieter side. Snow at the top in winter.

dientner-sattel.note: The saddle below the south face of the Hochkönig between Mühlbach and Dienten; with the Filzensattel the Hochkönig loop from Bischofshofen to Saalfelden. Short and steep, open all year.

edelweissspitze.classicAscent: 1.8 km, 10 % from the junction at the Fuscher Törl
edelweissspitze.note: A detour off the Großglockner High Alpine Road on the Fusch side: the Edelweißstraße, short, steep and cobbled, ends at the highest point of the toll road with a view of more than 30 three-thousanders. After snow it can stay closed longer than the main road.

faschinajoch.note: Short crossing from the Großes Walsertal to Damüls, usually ridden as the prelude to the Furkajoch. Cleared all year and the only winter access to Damüls.

filzensattel.classicAscent: 20 km, 3 % from Saalfelden via Maria Alm
filzensattel.note: The second saddle of the Hochkönig road, long and moderate from Saalfelden via Maria Alm and Hinterthal, short and steep from Dienten. Open all year.

flattnitz.note: A quiet alpine pass between the Gurk and Metnitz valleys in the Gurktal Alps, with a round church at the top. Steady on both sides, open all year.

flumserberg.note: From Flums steeply in hairpins up to the sunny terrace above the Walensee, with a view of the Churfirsten. Short and steep throughout, open all year.

foppolo.note: The hairpin road from the upper Brembo valley to the Foppolo ski resort at the head of the valley. Steady, cleared all year.

forcella-aurine.note: The crossing from Agordo via Voltago and Frassenè to Gosaldo, on the road to the Passo Cereda; open all year. Only the north side is a climb: from Gosaldo it is just 3.5 km and 155 m of ascent.

forcella-franche.note: The low crossing from Agordo via Rivamonte into the Valle del Mis; at the top the road to Gosaldo and the Passo Cereda branches off. The Agordo side is open all year; the valley road through the Valle del Mis with its partly unlit tunnels is officially closed in winter.

forcola-di-livigno.note: The border crossing between Livigno and the Bernina area, usually ridden as part of the loop over Bernina and Foscagno. High, bare and closed in winter.

fouillouse.classicAscent: 3.1 km, 10 % from the junction in the Ubaye valley
fouillouse.note: A detour in the upper Ubaye valley: the road climbs to the hamlet of Fouillouse below the Chambeyron massif. Not cleared in winter.

furkajoch.classicAscent: 21 km, 6.1 % from Rankweil through the Laterns valley
furkajoch.note: Narrow, little-used link from the Laternsertal to Damüls, closed in winter. A grassy crest at the top with views of the Rätikon and the Arlberg; the western ramp is tight and in places without a crash barrier.

furkapass.note: Winter closure usually late October/early November. Views of the Rhône Glacier and the Grimsel hairpins.

gaberl.note: The crossing of the Stubalpe between western Styria and the Mur valley, long and steady on both sides. Open all year.

gailbergsattel.note: The low crossing from the Drau valley into the Gail valley, short and even, with most of the hairpins on the north side. Cleared all year; ridden as the feeder to the Plöckenpass and on the loop around the Lienz Dolomites, so expect traffic on the B 110.

gaisberg.note: Salzburg's own mountain, from the old town via Guggenthal and the Zistelalm up to the summit with the transmitter; a classic of the Salzburg cycling scene. Open all year.

gampenjoch.note: From the Adige valley at Lana into the Nonsberg, even and without respite, hot lower down in summer. Main link into Trentino and cleared all year, so never entirely empty.

gargellen.note: A side valley of the Montafon up to the mountain village below the Swiss border, steady and quiet. Open all year.

gavarnie.note: The valley road through the Luz gorge to the village of Gavarnie in front of the famous cirque. Gentle, a lot of traffic in summer. Open all year.

gerlitzen.note: From the Ossiacher See via the Kanzelhöhe to just below the summit, the upper part as a toll road. 1,400 m of climbing, at the top the all-round view across the Carinthian lakes to the Julian Alps; closed in winter.

glaubenberg.note: The quiet neighbour of the Glaubenbielen, from Sarnen into the Entlebuch. Long ramps through forest, moorland at the top; closed in winter and hardly trafficked even in summer.

glaubenbielen.note: From Giswil on the Sarnersee up to Sörenberg, long and evenly steep. Wide alpine pastures at the top beneath the Brienzer Rothorn; closed in winter.

goldeck-panoramastrasse.classicAscent: 17 km, 9 % from Spittal an der Drau
goldeck-panoramastrasse.note: Toll road from Spittal to over 2,000 m below the Goldeck summit, 1,500 m of climbing with long steep ramps. At the top the view to the Tauern, the Dolomites and the Millstätter See; closed in winter.

gorges-de-daluis.note: Maintained all year, closed at times for rockfall. The red canyon of the Var, galleries and tunnels above the water; hardly any gradient, but uninterrupted scenery.

gorges-de-la-bourne.note: Maintained all year, closed at times for rockfall after rain and in spring. The road is blasted into the gorge wall for kilometres, single-track in places beneath overhanging rock; it is also the main approach to Villard-de-Lans.

gorges-de-la-nesque.note: Open all year. A balcony road climbing almost imperceptibly opposite the Rocher du Cire – the scenic way to ride to Sault for the Ventoux.

gorges-du-cians.note: Maintained all year, closed at times for rockfall. Red schist closing in above the road, narrow tunnels in between – one of the most impressive gorges of the Maritime Alps.

gorges-du-guil.note: Maintained all year, the gateway to the Queyras. Galleries and tunnels above the Guil; at the top the Izoard and the Agnel branch off.

gorges-du-nan.note: Maintained all year, closed at times for rockfall. Cut into the wall in 1894 without a parapet, three short unlit tunnels; the road does not end in Malleval but climbs on to the Col du Mont Noir.

gotthard-tremola.note: The cobbled Tremola hairpins. Pass road usually open until late October/November.

grand-ballon.note: The highest point of the Vosges a road reaches: 1343 m at the Col du Grand Ballon; the summit with its radar dome (1424 m) is a few minutes on foot. On the Tour de France route several times; the crest road over the top is closed in sections in winter.

grand-colombier.note: The king of the Jura: four ascents from the Rhône valley and the Valromey, at the top the view over the Lac du Bourget to Mont Blanc. A Tour de France finish in 2020 and 2023. Closed in winter.

grimselpass.note: Closure usually late October/November. Reservoirs and granite.

grosse-scheidegg.note: Car-free (PostBus only). Closure usually from late October. View of the Eiger north face.

grossglockner-hochalpenstrasse.classicAscent: 21 km, 8 % from Fusch to the Edelweißspitze
grossglockner-hochalpenstrasse.note: Toll road, scheduled to be open until late October/early November (closed at night, snow days possible). Bikes ride toll-free; the operator recommends riding before 7 am or after 3 pm. The top is the Hochtor (2504 m); the Edelweißspitze (2571 m) and the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe (2369 m) are detours, linked below the ascents.

gurnigelpass.note: The pass in the Gantrisch area between the Gürbe valley and the Schwarzsee region, more than 1,000 m from Wattenwil, at the top moorland and the view of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. Closed in winter.

haggenegg.note: A narrow crossing between Schwyz and the Alpthal below the Mythen, from Schwyz almost 900 m with long ramps over 10 %. The north side down to Alpthal is a narrow alp road; closed in winter.

hahntennjoch.classicAscent: 17 km, 5 % from Elmen (12 km, 7 % from Imst)
hahntennjoch.note: Winter closure usually from November, opens late in spring.

hautacam.note: The irregularly steep resort climb above Argelès, a Tour finish several times; at the top up to the Col de Tramassel. Cleared all year.

haute-vallee-de-cervieres.classicAscent: 11.5 km, 4 % from the junction in Cervières
haute-vallee-de-cervieres.note: A detour off the Izoard's north side: from Cervières the road runs gently up into the high valley behind it. Season window taken from the Col d'Izoard.

hintertux.note: From Mayrhofen in hairpins into the Tuxertal and up the valley to the foot of the Hintertux glacier. Steep at the bottom, moderate higher up; open all year, with traffic even in summer as a glacier ski area.

hochkar.note: Toll road up the Hochkar in the Mostviertel, with views across the Ybbstal Alps to the Ötscher. Steadily steep, the tarmac ends at the ski area on top; bikes pay no toll.

hochrindl.note: An alpine ridge with a holiday village between the Gurk valley and Reichenau; steep from Sirnitz, gentler from Ebene Reichenau. Open all year.

hochsoelden.classicAscent: 3.7 km, 11 % from the junction above Sölden
hochsoelden.note: A detour off the Ötztal glacier road: above Sölden the steep road to Hochsölden branches off.

hochtannbergpass.note: The crossing from the Bregenzerwald into the Lechtal, between Widderstein and Braunarlspitze. Cleared all year because Warth and Schröcken would otherwise have no connection – the avalanche slopes above are the reason for the galleries.

hohneck.note: A spur from the Route des Crêtes to just below one of the highest summits of the Vosges, with a view over the crest and the lakes. Closed in winter with the crest road.

hourquette-d-ancizan.note: The quiet alternative to the Aspin: a narrow road across wide pastures between the Aure valley and Payolle. Closed in winter.

ibergeregg.note: Between Schwyz and the Sihltal, steep and short. Cleared all year; at the top the view of the Mythen, which stand at your back for the whole climb.

iffigenalp.note: A single-lane mountain road from Lenk to the alp below the Wildstrubel, opened to cars in one direction at a time on a fixed schedule. Narrow and steep, closed in winter.

iselsberg.note: The B107 crossing from Lienz into the Möll valley at Winklern, and so the way to the Grossglockner road; cleared all year, with the traffic that brings, motorbikes and coaches included. The southern side via Dölsach is the longer one, with views of the Lienz Dolomites.

jaufenpass.note: Usually open into November. Third pass of the Ötztaler.

jaunpass.note: From the Simmental into the Gruyère country, the language border lies on the other side. Evenly steep through forest and pasture, cleared all year and lightly trafficked.

jochgrimm.classicAscent: 3.6 km, 6 % from the junction at the Lavazè
jochgrimm.note: A detour off the Lavazè pass: the road continues to the Jochgrimm (Passo Oclini) below the Schwarzhorn.

julierpass.note: Cleared all year, traffic heading for the Engadin.

kaiser-franz-josefs-hoehe.classicAscent: 8.6 km, 5.5 % from the junction in the Guttal
kaiser-franz-josefs-hoehe.note: A detour off the Großglockner High Alpine Road on the Carinthian side: the Gletscherstraße branches off in the Guttal and ends at the visitor centre facing the Großglockner, above the Pasterze glacier. Busy with day-trippers at the top, quieter early in the day.

kals-lucknerhaus.note: The dead-end road from Kals up to the Lucknerhaus, right beneath the south face of the Großglockner – the closest a road gets to Austria's highest mountain. Toll road for cars, bikes go free.

kartitscher-sattel.note: The valley watershed between the Pustertal and the Lesachtal, where the Gail rises: shorter and steep in places from Tassenbach, long and gentle from the Lesachtal. Cleared all year and quiet, a crossing through meadows below the Carnic Alps.

katschberg.classicAscent: 6 km, 9.6 % from St. Michael im Lungau
katschberg.note: The old road between the Lungau and the Lieser valley, short on both sides with ramps of up to 20 %, one of the steepest pass roads in the Alps; the motorway runs in a tunnel underneath. Open all year.

kaunertaler-gletscherstrasse.note: From the Kaunertal past the Gepatsch reservoir to the end of the public road at 2,510 m – the final hairpins to the glacier car park at around 2,750 m are an access road of the ski area. Toll road: cars pay, bikes ride free. Thin air at the top, hairpins far above the tree line.

kesselberg.note: The hairpin road between the Kochelsee and the Walchensee, a racing circuit since 1897 and a motorcycle magnet to this day – correspondingly loud on fine weekends. Short, but the view of the Walchensee from above carries it.

kitzbueheler-horn.note: Dead-end road, usually rideable well into late autumn. Short and very steep. Toll road for cars, bikes ride free.

klippitztoerl.note: The crossing of the Saualpe between the Lavant and Görtschitz valleys, steady on both sides. At the top pastures and a small ski area; open all year.

kolm-saigurn.note: Up the Rauris valley to its head below the Hoher Sonnblick, a quiet side valley of the Tauern. Long and moderate, steeper only in the last kilometres.

kuehtai.note: Open all year, first climb of the Ötztaler Radmarathon.

l-ecot.note: A detour at the foot of the Iseran's south side: from Bonneval-sur-Arc the road leads to the hamlet of L'Écot at the head of the Haute-Maurienne valley. Season window taken from the Iseran.

la-plagne.note: Road to a ski resort, cleared all year. In 2025 the finish of stage 19 of the Tour de France and of the Étape du Tour, at Plagne Villages above Plagne Centre; a long, steady climb, rather plain to look at.

la-planche-des-belles-filles.note: A Tour de France finish since 2012, and in 2020 the time trial with which Pogačar won the Tour. The tarmac ends at the ski station; the gravel ramp of the “Super Planche” above it is no place for a road bike.

la-toussuire.note: The ski resort above Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne, a Tour de France finish in 2012; from Saint-Jean via Fontcouverte in hairpins up the slope. Cleared all year.

lac-de-cap-de-long.note: Through the Couplan valley into the Néouvielle up to the Cap-de-Long dam at over 2,100 m, a granite landscape with lakes at the top. Closed above Fabian in winter.

lac-de-moiry.classicAscent: 32 km, 5.3 % from Sierre via Vissoie and Grimentz
lac-de-moiry.note: Through the Val d'Anniviers via Vissoie and Grimentz up to the dam, more than 1,700 m of climbing in one go. At the top a turquoise reservoir below the Moiry glacier; closed above Grimentz in winter.

le-chazelet.note: Short dead end above La Grave; at the top you stand face to face with the Meije – one of the great panoramas of the Western Alps. Continuing onto the Plateau d'Emparis is only possible off the tarmac.

le-markstein.note: Ski station where the crest road meets the D430 from the Florival and the D27 from the upper Thur valley; a Tour de France stage finish in 2023. The access roads to the station are cleared in winter, while the Route des Crêtes to the north and on to the Grand Ballon is closed then.

lenzerheide.note: The main road from Chur into the Albula valley via Churwalden, Valbella and the Heidsee, the approach to the Albula and the Julier and so busy; open all year. From Chur in hairpins and steep for a long way, from Tiefencastel via Lantsch more even.

les-arcs.note: Ski-resort ascent via Arc 1800, open all year. Sober scenery, useful as training for the metres of climbing.

les-deux-alpes.note: The hairpin climb from the Romanche valley to the ski resort, a Tour finish in 1998. Shorter than Alpe d'Huez and with more traffic to the resort. Cleared all year.

leukerbad.note: From Susten via Leuk and high above the Dala gorge to the spa town below the Gemmi wall; steady, with a few hairpins. Open all year.

loiblpass.note: Through traffic takes the tunnel below, which is why the old pass road over the top is quiet – and steep: over 20 % on the south side. At the northern portal stands the memorial to the Loibl concentration camp sub-camp.

loser-panoramastrasse.note: Steep toll road above the Altausseer See into the Totes Gebirge, with ramps around 16 %. Cars are charged, bikes ride free; at the top the tarmac ends on the Loser plateau with views across the Ausseerland.

luenersee.classicAscent: 18 km, 5.6 % from Bludenz through the Brandnertal
luenersee.note: Up the Brandnertal from Bludenz via Brand to the valley station of the Lünersee cable car below the Schesaplana, the last stretch narrow and steep. Closed beyond Brand in winter.

lukmanierpass.note: Closure weather-dependent from November, often open longer than its neighbours.

luz-ardiden.note: The hairpin road from Luz to the ski resort, a Tour finish several times. At the top a cascade of hairpins on open slopes. Cleared all year.

macugnaga.note: Through the Valle Anzasca from Piedimulera to Macugnaga below the east face of the Monte Rosa, the highest wall in the Alps. Long and moderately steep, open all year.

madonna-del-colletto.note: The saddle with the little sanctuary between the Stura and Gesso valleys, the last climb of the Granfondo Fausto Coppi. Short, steep and almost traffic-free; the surface on the Festiona side is old and often gritty.

madonna-del-ghisallo.note: The patron saint of cyclists stands in the chapel at the top, the cycling museum beside it – not a high pass, but the most famous climb in Lombardy. Steep from Bellagio above Lake Como, a fixture of the Giro di Lombardia.

malbun.note: Liechtenstein's climb: steeply in hairpins from Vaduz to Triesenberg with a view across the Rhine valley, then through the tunnel to Steg and up to the ski village of Malbun. Steep throughout, open all year.

malojapass.note: Open all year; wall of hairpins right at the top, a long valley before it.

malta-hochalmstrasse.note: Toll road to the Kölnbrein reservoir, scheduled to be open until mid/late October. Bikes ride toll-free.

mangart-sattel.note: Slovenia's highest road, a dead end, usually open until late October. The ride now ends at the car park at just over 1900 m: the loop up to the saddle is closed.

martelltal.classicAscent: 25.5 km, 5.5 % from Goldrain to the Enzianhütte
martelltal.note: From the Vinschgau past the Zufrittsee to beneath the north faces of the Cevedale – a dead end that climbs 1,400 m and gets properly steep in the final stretch. At the top the tarmac ends at the Enzianhütte car park.

melchsee-frutt.classicAscent: 19 km, 6.9 % from Kerns through the Melchtal
melchsee-frutt.note: Through the Melchtal to Stöckalp and then up the narrow toll road with ramps of up to 15 % to the plateau at the Melchsee. 1,350 m of climbing, at the top mountain lakes at 1,900 m; the upper part closed in winter.

mendelpass.note: From the vineyards above Kaltern up the Mendel wall in tight hairpins, looking back across the Adige valley as far as the Rosengarten. Cleared all year and busy as the link into the Nonsberg.

meribel-mottaret.classicAscent: 14.7 km, 3 % from the junction in Méribel
meribel-mottaret.note: A detour off the Loze climb from Brides-les-Bains: the road continues through Méribel to the ski village of Mottaret. Season window taken from the Col de la Loze.

mont-crosin.note: The short pass between Saint-Imier and Tramelan across the pastures with the wind turbines of Mont-Soleil. Open all year.

mont-du-chat.note: The southernmost Jura pass right above the Lac du Bourget: from the east 13 km at a steady 9 %, crossed by the Tour de France in 2017. The west side from Yenne is gentler.

mont-revard.note: The home climb of Aix-les-Bains: more than 1,200 m from the lakeshore through forest onto the plateau, at the top the view across the Lac du Bourget to Mont Blanc. Open all year.

mont-ventoux.note: Summit road usually not closed until mid-November. October is ideal, but the Mistral can be brutal; check the wind forecast.

montagne-de-lure.note: The 'little Ventoux': from Saint-Étienne-les-Orgues through forest to just below the Signal de Lure, at the top a panorama from the Écrins to the Ventoux. Closed above the resort in winter.

monte-beigua.note: From Varazze via Alpicella to the highest point of the Ligurian coastal mountains, the road ends at the antennas with a view from the sea to the Alps. Open all year; often windy at the top.

monte-bignone.note: The mountain above Sanremo: from the harbour through the villas, via San Romolo and the hairpins to the end of the tarmac a good 1,000 m above the sea; the summit above belongs to the antennas and a gravel track. Open all year and the longest ascent on the Riviera dei Fiori.

monte-bisbino.note: From Lake Como at Cernobbio through 17 km of forest to the summit with its pilgrimage church, the view reaches over the whole southern part of the lake to Milan. The home climb of the Como cyclists; often snow at the top in winter.

monte-bondone.note: Trento's home mountain, a Giro climb since 1956 – the stage Charly Gaul won in a snowstorm. Over 1,400 m of climbing in one go from the Adige, cleared all year as far as the ski area.

monte-ceneri.note: The low crossing between Sopraceneri and Sottoceneri, relieved since the base tunnel but still a through road. Not a destination in itself, but the link between Locarno and Lugano, open all year.

monte-generoso-bellavista.note: The road ends at the Bellavista station of the Generoso railway, 900 m above Lake Lugano; the summit is left to the train and the walkers. Steep and quiet from Rovio, with the lake at your back. Snow at the top in winter.

monte-pizzoc.classicAscent: 4.0 km, 6 % from the junction on the Cansiglio
monte-pizzoc.note: A detour off the Cansiglio plateau: the road climbs to the top of Monte Pizzoc with a view over the Venetian plain.

monte-san-primo.note: Beyond the Ghisallo and on from Magreglio to the Parco Monte San Primo, where the tarmac ends: the highest point of the Larian Triangle, with Lake Como on both sides. Snow at the top in winter.

monte-velo.note: From Arco up to the alpine pastures above the Sarca valley, where the tarmac ends at the meadows of Monte Velo; Lake Garda lies far below to the south. The home climb of the Arco climbers on a road bike; snow at the top in winter.

monte-zoncolan.note: Usually rideable well into late autumn. The steepest Giro classic.

monte-zugna.classicAscent: 12.1 km, 7 % from the junction in Albaredo
monte-zugna.note: A detour at the Pian delle Fugazze: from Albaredo near Rovereto the road climbs a long way to Monte Zugna, a First World War site. Not cleared in winter.

moosalp.note: The link from the Visp valley to the Rhône valley over an alp with larches and mountain lakes, at the top the view of the Weisshorn, the Mischabel and the Bernese Alps. From Stalden via Törbel short and steep, from Raron via Unterbäch and Bürchen longer and more even; closed in winter.

mottarone.note: The viewpoint mountain between Lake Maggiore and Lake Orta, a Giro summit finish in 2009. The free ascent comes from Armeno via Gignese; the road from Stresa is a private toll road. Usually snow at the top from December to March.

muro-di-sormano.note: Two kilometres at an average of 15 % with ramps up to 27 %, the gradient percentages painted on the tarmac. Dropped from the Giro di Lombardia in 1962 because hardly anyone made it up riding; back in the race since 2012.

nassfeldpass.note: The northern ramp from Tröpolach is one of the hardest ascents in Carinthia, with ramps over 17 % in the lower part. A ski resort on the border at the top; cleared all year.

nevegal.note: Belluno's home climb: from the town via Castion to the small resort on the Col Visentin, at the top the view of the Belluno Dolomites. Cleared all year.

nigerpass.note: The quiet side door to the Rosengarten: steep and shaded up from Tiers, and at the top the wall stands right above the road. Cleared all year, but only a feeder – through traffic takes the Karerpass.

nockalmstrasse.note: Toll road (Eisentalhöhe), scheduled to be open until late October. Bikes ride toll-free.

norbertshoehe.note: From Martina on the Swiss border up in hairpins onto the Nauders plateau, even and well built; open all year and the cyclists' way towards the Reschen, because the B 180 through the Finstermünz gorge is closed to bikes. Single-sided, since Nauders lies barely lower than the top; when the B 180 is closed completely, bikes are banned uphill here as well.

nufenenpass.note: Highest Swiss road pass lying entirely within the country. Closure usually mid/late October.

oberalppass.note: Closure usually from November. Lighthouse at the top.

oberjoch.note: The Jochstraße from Bad Hindelang packs 106 hairpins into a few kilometres – Germany's twistiest road. Main link into the Tannheimer Tal and correspondingly busy, cleared all year.

oetztaler-gletscherstrasse.note: Austria's highest tarmac road (Tiefenbach tunnel). Closures at short notice in snow, skiing in operation at the top. Toll road for cars, bikes ride free.

ofenpass.note: Open all year, through the National Park.

orcieres-merlette.note: Tour finish in 1971 and 2020, otherwise a quiet ski resort in the Champsaur. Even gradient, hardly any traffic outside the season.

pass-thurn.note: The link from Kitzbühel into the upper Pinzgau, a wide main road with traffic. From Mittersill in hairpins with a view of the Hohe Tauern, flat from Jochberg; open all year.

passo-brocon.note: Between Valsugana and Primiero, a pass without an audience: wide meadows, hardly any cars, the Pale di San Martino in view to the north. Cleared all year for the small ski area.

passo-campolongo.note: Open all year, the lowest Sellaronda pass.

passo-cereda.note: The crossing from Primiero to Agordo, beneath the south faces of the Pale. Short and good-natured, usually ridden as a feeder between two bigger passes; cleared all year.

passo-cibiana.note: The quiet crossing between the Cadore and the Zoldo valley, beneath the north face of Monte Rite. Hardly any traffic, Reinhold Messner's Museum in the Clouds at the top; cleared all year.

passo-cimabanche.note: The flat valley crossing between Toblach and Cortina, past the Toblacher See and the Dürrensee with Monte Cristallo and the view into the valley of the Drei Zinnen. Open all year and busy, lorries included; quieter is the cycle path on the old railway line beside it, partly gravel on the Toblach side.

passo-croce-d-aune.note: From Pedavena near Feltre in hairpins up through the forest to the saddle where, as the legend goes, Tullio Campagnolo failed with numb fingers at his rear wheel and invented the quick release; a monument at the top recalls it. Open all year and quiet, to the west through the villages of Sovramonte.

passo-crocedomini.note: Lonely, coarse tarmac in places. Closure usually from November.

passo-d-ampola.note: The flat crossing at the end of the Ledro valley to Storo: from Molina along the lake, hardly any gradient, then down into the Chiese valley. Not a mountain, a valley; open all year. Up from Riva runs the car-free Ponale road, which no router knows as a road – so the ascent only starts at Molina.

passo-d-eira.note: The smaller of the two passes separating Livigno from the Valtellina – right before the Foscagno. Short and usually ridden only in passing; busy because of duty-free Livigno.

passo-del-ballino.note: From Riva via Tenno and past the Lago di Tenno onto the Fiavè plateau: the classic way in from Lake Garda to the Trentino, open all year and with traffic at weekends.

passo-del-cason-di-lanza.note: A narrow mountain pass in the Carnic Alps between Paularo and Pontebba, at the top pastures below the Monte Zermula. Closed in winter.

passo-del-faiallo.note: From the sea at Genoa-Voltri via Mele and the Acquasanta monastery onto the crest of the Ligurian Alps; at the top the coast lies 1,000 m below in the haze, the Po plain behind. The top of the road lies a few hundred metres from the actual saddle. Open all year, briefly closed after snowfall in winter.

passo-del-foscagno.note: Open all year (access road to Livigno).

passo-del-ginestro.note: The quiet neighbour of the Colle San Bartolomeo, open all year: up from Chiusanico through olives and broom, a view of both valleys at the top, down to Cesio in the Arroscia valley.

passo-del-maniva.note: Long ascent from the Val Trompia or from Bagolino, with a ridge road at the top and views as far as Lake Garda. Closed in winter, very quiet in summer.

passo-del-mortirolo.note: Rideable almost all year, a forest road without views, but mercilessly steep.

passo-del-redebus.note: The quiet crossing from the Valsugana at Pergine into the Fersina valley and onto the Piné plateau. Forest, pastures and hardly any traffic. Open all year.

passo-del-tonale.note: Open all year, often combined with the Gavia or the Mortirolo.

passo-del-turchino.note: The pass where Milan–Sanremo reaches the sea: after 140 km of flat the first climb, the short tunnel at the top, then the view of the Riviera. Unspectacular as a road and with traffic; as a place, cycling history. Open all year.

passo-del-vivione.note: One of the quietest roads in the Bergamasque Alps, narrow and without crash barriers above the Val di Scalve. Closed in winter; anyone looking for traffic is in the wrong place.

passo-dell-aprica.note: The main link between the Valtellina and the Val Camonica, with traffic to match – the pass appears regularly in the Giro, usually as the approach to the Mortirolo or the Gavia. Even and never steep.

passo-della-mauria.note: The crossing from the Cadore into Friuli at the springs of the Tagliamento, moderate on both sides and through forest. Open all year.

passo-della-presolana.note: The crossing from the Val Seriana into the Val di Scalve below the limestone walls of the Presolana, the 'queen of the Bergamasque Alps'. Steady from Clusone, shorter and steeper from Dezzo. Open all year.

passo-delle-erbe.classicAscent: 12 km, 7 % from St. Martin in Thurn
passo-delle-erbe.note: Peitlerkofel views, closure usually from November.

passo-delle-fittanze.note: From the Adige valley at Ala via Sega di Ala onto the crest of the Lessinia: 1,200 m of climbing with long ramps around 10 %, karst and pasture at the top. The south side is the Erbezzo plateau, not a climb. Closed in winter.

passo-dello-stelvio.note: Closure between mid-October and late November, depending on the winter. The first half of October is often ideal, after that it is a lottery.

passo-di-agueglio.note: From Lake Como at Varenna up via Perledo and Esino Lario and down to Parlasco in the Valsassina; the lake side with its view of Bellagio is the beautiful one. Snow at the top in winter.

passo-di-campogrosso.note: From Recoaro Terme to beneath the walls of the Little Dolomites, steep and shady up to the summit with its rifugio. Tarmac from the south only: the north side to the Pian delle Fugazze is a gravel road. Closed in winter.

passo-di-costalunga.note: The main link from the Eggental into the Val di Fassa, cleared all year and correspondingly busy. Short and even; the Karersee and the Rosengarten wall just below the summit are the reason to ride up here all the same.

passo-di-gavia.note: Often closed as early as early/mid-October. Narrow, wild road; make use of a weather window.

passo-di-valcava.note: From Torre de' Busi one of the steepest climbs in northern Italy: 1,000 m of climbing at a double-digit average with ramps up to 17 %. Giro passage in 2008. The east side from the Valle Imagna is the tame one; snow at the top in winter.

passo-duran.note: Open all year, steep sections up to 15 %.

passo-fedaia.note: Usually open all year. Marmolada views, brutal finale from Malga Ciapela.

passo-furcia.note: The ramp from the Pustertal to St. Vigil in Enneberg, the shortest way into the Dolomites from the north. Steadily steep through forest, with the Kronplatz above the road at the top; cleared all year.

passo-giau.note: Usually open into November. Perhaps the most beautiful pass in the Dolomites.

passo-lavaze.note: From the Val di Fiemme up to the plateau between Latemar and Schwarzhorn, wide meadows at the top rather than rock. Cleared all year, a cross-country skiing centre in winter.

passo-manghen.note: Narrow, steep, hardly any traffic. Closure usually from November.

passo-pampeago.note: The steep climb from Tesero to the Alpe di Pampeago ski station, where the Giro has finished several times; the last three kilometres to the pass were only paved in 2012 and are closed to cars, the road down to Obereggen is single-track. In winter the top lies inside the ski area; it is a summer road.

passo-pordoi.note: Usually open all year (closed only in snow). Part of the Sellaronda.

passo-rest.note: A remote forest pass between the Tagliamento and the Tramonti valleys, almost deserted on both sides. Open all year.

passo-san-bernardino.note: Old pass road alongside the motorway. Closure usually from November.

passo-san-boldo.note: The "Road of a Hundred Days", built into the wall by forced labour in 1918: five hairpin tunnels stacked on top of each other, the hairpins themselves inside the rock. Low and open all year, with traffic lights in the single-track tunnels.

passo-san-marco.note: Quiet road in the Bergamo Alps, closure usually from November.

passo-sant-antonio.note: The steep short cut from Auronzo into the Comelico, almost entirely in forest and lightly used; from Padola only a short counter-climb. No winter closure known; the pass is low and links two valley villages.

passo-santa-barbara.note: From Rovereto through the hairpins above Isera to the crossing into the Val di Gresta, crossed by the Giro in 2025. The west side from Nago via Ronzo is the quieter one. Snow at the top in winter.

passo-sella.note: Usually open all year. Right beneath the Sella towers.

passo-sommo.note: From the Adige valley at Calliano via Folgaria onto the Vigolana plateau; the climb is the hairpin road up to Folgaria, the pass beyond it no more than a hill. Cleared all year.

passo-teglia.note: The highest tarmac crossing in the Sanremo hinterland, between the Argentina valley and Rezzo. Hardly any traffic, chestnut forest, pasture and ridge at the top. Open all year, at times not after snowfall in January and February.

passo-tre-croci.note: The short crossing from Cortina to Misurina, usually ridden as the approach to the Tre Cime. Even through forest, with views of Sorapiss and Cristallo at the top; cleared all year.

passo-tremalzo.classicAscent: 13.0 km, 7 % from the junction in the Val di Ledro
passo-tremalzo.note: A detour from the Val di Ledro: the paved road climbs to the Passo Tremalzo; beyond it only gravel continues towards Lake Garda. Not cleared in winter.
ascents: Junction in the Val di Ledro

passo-valles.note: Links the Biois valley with the Travignolo valley and is usually strung together with Rolle and San Pellegrino into a loop. Narrow, little traffic, the final kilometres above the tree line.

passo-valparola.note: Open all year, right next to the Falzarego.

passo-vezzena.note: From Lake Caldonazzo through the hairpins of the Menador onto the plateau of Lavarone and Asiago; the north side is the climb, the south side from the Asiago plateau barely one. Cleared all year.

passo-xomo.note: The little neighbour of the Fugazze above Valli del Pasubio, short and steep, with the Strada degli Scarubbi as its gravel continuation towards the Pasubio. Quiet on the Posina side. Open all year, not after snowfall in winter.

passwang.note: The crossing from the Thal into the Lüssel valley in the Solothurn Jura, through the short summit tunnel at the top. Open all year.

pavlicevo-sedlo.note: The small border pass between the Logar valley and Bad Eisenkappel below the Kamnik–Savinja Alps, quiet on both sides. Often closed in winter.

penegal.classicAscent: 3.8 km, 9 % from the top of the Mendel Pass
penegal.note: A detour off the top of the Mendel Pass: the road climbs through the forest to the lookout tower on the Penegal, with a view over the Adige valley to the Dolomites.

penserjoch.note: Closure usually from November, little traffic.

pfaender.note: Bregenz's own mountain, from the town via Fluh to just below the summit, with a view over the whole of Lake Constance. Short and steadily steep, open all year.

pian-del-re.note: The road through the upper Po valley to the source of the Po right below the north face of the Monviso. Gentle as far as Crissolo, then narrow and steep. Closed above Crissolo in winter; at times closed to cars on summer weekends.

pian-delle-fugazze.note: The crossing from the Adige valley into the Val Leogra beneath the Pasubio, a World War front line and Giro passage. Long from Rovereto through the Vallarsa, short and steep from Valli del Pasubio. Cleared all year.

piani-dei-resinelli.note: From Ballabio in hairpins to beneath the walls of the Grigna, the road ends on the Resinelli plateau with a view of Lecco and the lake. Steep and shady; snow at the top in winter.

pila.note: From Aosta via Gressan in long hairpins up to the ski station above the town, steadily steep from bottom to top. At the top the view across the whole valley to Mont Blanc; open all year.

piller-sattel.note: The quiet link from the Pitztal into the upper Inn valley across a high moorland. Steady from Wenns, short and very steep down to Fließ; at the top, at the Gacher Blick, a view far into the Inn valley. Open all year.

pitztal-mittelberg.note: The Pitztal ends after twenty flat kilometres at the glacier car park in Mittelberg, beneath the Wildspitze. Little gradient, little traffic; cleared all year because of the glacier ski area.

pla-d-adet.note: The ski resort above Saint-Lary, a Tour finish several times; steep ramps at the bottom via Soulan. Cleared all year.

plateau-de-beille.note: The long, steadily steep climb to the cross-country ski centre, a Tour finish several times. 15 km at 8 % without a break. Cleared all year.

plateau-des-glieres.note: Ascent to the plateau with the 1944 Resistance memorial; the through road ends at the top. The Tour went up in 2018 and 2020.

ploeckenpass.note: The old Roman link from Carinthia to Carnia, an open-air museum of the mountain war at the top. The southern ramp steepens to over 10 % in the final kilometres; cleared all year, closed at times for rockfall.

plose.note: Brixen's home climb: via St. Andrä and Palmschoss almost 1,450 m up to the Kreuztal below the Plose summit, at the top the view of the Odle (Geisler) peaks. Cleared all year.

poggio-di-sanremo.note: The last four uphill kilometres of Milan–Sanremo: 160 m above the sea, greenhouses, four hairpins and the village at the top, then the descent into the Via Roma. Open all year and ridden every day by road bikes re-enacting the sprint.

pokljuka.note: The road from Bled onto the forested Pokljuka plateau to the Rudno polje biathlon centre, on the edge of Triglav National Park. Steady, cleared all year.

port-d-envalira.note: The highest road pass in the Pyrenees, between Andorra and France. Moderately steep, but a main road with heavy traffic and petrol stations; the tunnel takes part of it. Cleared all year.

port-de-bales.note: The wild pass between the Barousse and the Luchon valley, in the Tour route since 2007. Long from the north with steep sections in the upper part, narrow. Closed in winter.

port-de-la-bonaigua.note: The high pass between the Val d'Aran and the Pallars, over 2,000 m with wide hairpins on the east side. Cleared, closed at times after snowfall.

port-de-lers.note: The pass at the Étang de Lers between the Vicdessos valley and Massat, ridden together with the Col d'Agnes. Closed at times after snowfall.

port-del-canto.note: The long crossing between the Pallars and the Alt Urgell, more than 1,000 m on both sides. Cleared all year.

postalm.classicAscent: 27.7 km, 2.8 % from Strobl into the Lammertal
postalm.note: Austria's largest high alpine pasture, reached by a toll road from Strobl on the Wolfgangsee – bikes pay nothing. Wide pastures without forest at the top; the road runs almost level across the plateau for a long way and then drops into the Lammertal.

pra-loup.note: In 1975 Merckx cracked here and Thévenet won the Tour. Short, even, with views into the Ubaye valley.

praebichl.note: The pass between Eisenerz and Vordernberg, with the stepped mountain of the Erzberg beside the road. Short and steady on both sides; open all year.

pragelpass.note: Between the Muotatal and the Klöntal, closed to cars on Sundays and public holidays – then the road belongs to the bikes. Narrow, steep and with the Klöntalersee as the reward on the east side.

prato-nevoso.note: The ski resort above Frabosa in the Ligurian Alps, a Tour de France finish in 2008. Short and steadily steep through chestnut forest. Cleared all year.

predilpass.note: From Tarvisio past the Raibler See to Bovec in the Soča valley, usually ridden together with the Vršič. The southern ramp drops steeply into the Soča; at the top the remains of the Habsburg blocking fort.

punta-veleno.note: From the shore of Lake Garda at Brenzone up to the Punta Veleno on Monte Baldo: a good nine kilometres at eleven percent on average with ramps up to 20 %, the steepest climb on the lake. At the top the road tips over towards Prada Alta. The poison in the name is well earned; snow at the top in winter.

radstaedter-tauernpass.note: The pass over Obertauern between the Enns valley and the Lungau, the old Roman road beside the Tauern motorway. Long from Radstadt with a steep stretch before Untertauern, steady from Mauterndorf; open all year.

reschenpass.note: From Mals across the Malser Haide and along the Haidersee and the Reschensee, with the church tower in the lake just before the top; a wide transit road, open all year. South side only: from the north the B 180 between Kajetansbrücke and Nauders is closed to bikes, the cycle route comes via Martina and the Norbertshöhe, and from Nauders only about 100 m of climbing remain.

rhemes-notre-dame.classicAscent: 14.2 km, 5 % from the junction near Introd
rhemes-notre-dame.note: A detour at the entrance of the Valsavarenche: near Introd the Val di Rhêmes branches off, and the road ends in Rhêmes-Notre-Dame.

riale.note: Through the Valle Antigorio and the Val Formazza from Crodo to the Toce waterfall and the high plain of Riale. Long and flat at the bottom, at the top in hairpins beside the fall; open to Riale all year.

riedbergpass.note: Germany's highest pass road and, at 16 % in the upper third, one of its steepest too. Links the Iller valley with Balderschwang; cleared all year, at times chains only during heavy snowfall.

rifugio-dei-forni.note: A detour off the Gavia climb from Bormio: in Santa Caterina the narrow road branches off into the Valle dei Forni and ends at the hut below the Forni glacier. Season window taken from the Gavia.

risoul.note: The hairpin road from Guillestre to the Risoul resort, a Tour de France finish in 2014. Steady, at the top larches and the view of the Pelvoux. Cleared all year.

rittner-hochplateau.note: The sun terrace above Bozen: after the hairpins out of the Adige valley the road runs almost level across meadows and larches, with the Rosengarten and the Schlern opposite. Cleared all year, hardly any through traffic at the top.

rossfeld-panoramastrasse.note: Germany's highest high road, toll, cleared all year. Cars are charged, bikes ride free.

route-de-presles.note: Maintained all year, closed at times for rockfall. A handful of tunnels and a ribbon of road hanging free above the walls of Choranche; at the top it ends in the village.

route-des-cretes.classicAscent: 29 km from the Col de la Schlucht to the Grand Ballon
route-des-cretes.note: The crest road of the high Vosges, built as a supply road in the First World War: over grassy domes with views of the Rhine plain and, on a clear day, the Alps; the Tour de France rides stretches of it too, such as from the Markstein to the Grand Ballon. Closed in winter roughly mid-November to mid-April; lots of motorbikes at weekends.

saanenmoeser.note: The flat crossing from the Simmental into the Saanenland towards Gstaad, a main road beside the railway. Short and gentle, open all year.

saas-fee.note: Up the Saas valley to the edge of the car-free village, at the end below the glaciers of the Dom and the Allalin. At the bottom the valley road with the traffic to the Saas villages, steeper in hairpins from Saas-Grund; open all year.

saint-veran.classicAscent: 5.1 km, 5 % from the junction near Molines
saint-veran.note: A detour off the Agnello climb from the Queyras: the road branches off near Molines and ends in Saint-Véran, one of the highest villages in Europe.

samnaun.note: From the Inn at Vinadi through tunnels and galleries into the duty-free high valley of Samnaun. Steady, open all year.

santuario-di-oropa.note: From Biella through forest to the great pilgrimage site below Monte Mucrone, steeper at the top. A Giro d'Italia finish several times, known for Pantani's comeback ride in 1999; open all year.

santuario-di-sant-anna-di-vinadio.classicAscent: 2.8 km, 9 % from the junction on the Lombarde road
santuario-di-sant-anna-di-vinadio.note: A detour off the Italian side of the Lombarde: the road branches off below the pass and ends at the highest sanctuary in Europe. Season window taken from the Lombarde.
