sattelegg.note: The crossing from the end of Lake Zurich to the Sihlsee, long from Siebnen via Vorderthal, short from Euthal. Open all year.

sauris.note: Through the Lumiei gorge with its partly unlit tunnels to the turquoise Sauris reservoir and up to the German-speaking village of Sauris di Sopra. Open all year.

schallenberg.note: The crossing from Lake Thun into the Emmental and the Entlebuch, gentle on both sides and over hills with farms. Open all year.

schnalstal-kurzras.note: From Naturns up to 2,000 m at the glacier, the whole valley a single dead end. Long and even, the Ötzi find site lies above the head of the valley; cleared all year because of the glacier ski area.

schoeckl.classicAscent: 26 km, 4.1 % from Graz-Andritz via St. Radegund
schoeckl.note: Graz's own mountain, from Andritz via St. Radegund up to the summit plateau; the last kilometres narrow and steep. Open all year.

schwaegalp.note: The summit lies right beneath the north face of the Säntis, which carries the climb – the wall stands above the road for the last few kilometres. Cleared all year, starting point of the Säntis cable car.

seebergsattel.note: The quiet border crossing between the Karawanks and the Kamnik Alps, east of the Loibl. Even and little used, meadows rather than rock at the top; cleared all year.

seefelder-sattel.classicAscent: 10.5 km, 5.6 % from Zirl via the Zirler Berg
seefelder-sattel.note: The main road from Innsbruck to Seefeld and Garmisch, from Zirl the notorious Zirler Berg at 16 % – wide, but with a lot of traffic. From Scharnitz barely any gradient; open all year.

seiser-alm.note: Europe's largest high alpine pasture, with the Schlern and the Langkofel as a backdrop. The ascent from Seis is closed to cars on weekdays from 9 to 17, open to bikes throughout – the closure hours are exactly the time you want to ride here.

sella-nevea.note: The saddle between Kanin and Montasch, reached via Cave del Predil. Very quiet, high walls on both sides; cleared all year for the ski area.

selvino.note: The home climb of the Bergamasques: 21 hairpins from Nembro up to the village on the plateau, since Felice Gimondi the road where everyone here learns to ride. Cleared all year; the continuation via Aviatico into the Val Serina makes the loop.

semnoz.note: From the lakeshore up to the Crêt de Châtillon, with a panorama from the Bauges to Mont Blanc at the top. Tour finish in 2013; closed above the alpine pasture in winter.

sestriere.note: The ski resort on the summit between the Val Chisone and the Val Susa, a Giro and Tour regular since the 1930s – Coppi and Pantani have won here. Cleared all year; plain as scenery, heavy with history.

sighignola.note: The Balcone d'Italia: the road ends at the Swiss border on a ledge 1,000 m above Lake Lugano, with Lugano and the four-thousanders of the Valais in view. Quiet and even from the Val d'Intelvi; not cleared at the top in winter.

silvretta-hochalpenstrasse.note: Toll road, usually open until late October. Bielerhöhe with its reservoir. Bikes ride toll-free.

simplonpass.note: Open all year, wide road with traffic.

soelkpass.classicAscent: 15 km, 6.5 % from Stein an der Enns
soelkpass.note: Closure usually from November, little traffic.

sommet-bucher.note: A detour in the Queyras: from Ville-Vieille a narrow paved forest road climbs through the larches to the lookout summit above Château-Queyras. Not cleared in winter.

soriska-planina.note: The crossing from the Bohinj into the Selška valley over a small ski pasture, in hairpins on the Bohinj side, long via the village of Sorica on the east side. Open all year.

spitzingsattel.classicAscent: 9.3 km, 3.7 % from Schliersee, the top 2.5 km steep
spitzingsattel.note: From Schliersee via Neuhaus and the steep ramp up to the saddle above the Spitzingsee, beyond which the road drops to the lake and ends. Short, open all year, day-trip traffic at weekends.

spluegenpass.classicAscent: 9 km, 8 % from Splügen (30 km from Chiavenna)
spluegenpass.note: The Italian south ramp with its wall of hairpins is a highlight. Closure usually from November.

sportgastein.note: The Gasteiner Alpenstraße ends at the head of the Nassfeld valley beneath the three-thousanders of the Goldberg group. Toll road – cars are charged, bikes ride free; at the top nothing but a ski lift, meadows and the old gold mines.

staffal.note: Up the long Lys valley from Pont-Saint-Martin through the Walser villages of Gressoney-Saint-Jean and Gressoney-La-Trinité to the head of the valley below the Monte Rosa. Long and flat at the bottom, steeper at the top; open all year.

staller-sattel.note: Above the Antholzer See from the Pustertal into the Defereggental, high and very quiet. The southern ramp is single-track and run as a one-way system: one direction per hour, switching on the half hour – check the time windows before riding.

stoderzinken.note: Toll road from Gröbming up to the alp below the summit, steep and narrow, at the top the view across the Enns valley to the Tauern. Closed in winter.

strada-della-forra.note: From Lake Garda into the Brasa gorge, kilometres beneath overhanging rock and through unlit tunnels, then out onto the plateau of Tremosine. Open all year, narrow and busy in summer – Winston Churchill called it the eighth wonder of the world.

stubaital.note: Up the whole Stubaital from Schönberg via Fulpmes and Neustift to the valley station of the glacier lift. Long and moderate, steeper only in the last kilometres beyond Ranalt; open all year, busy at the bottom.

sudelfeld.note: From the Leitzach valley across the ski slopes of the Sudelfeld over into the Inn valley; the eastern ramp is named Tatzelwurm after the waterfall. Cleared all year and full of motorcycles at weekends.

sulden.classicAscent: 9.2 km, 7 % from the junction in Gomagoi
sulden.note: A detour off the Stelvio climb from Prad: in Gomagoi the road branches off into the Sulden valley and ends in the village below the Ortler.

superbagneres.note: The road from Luchon to the Grand Hôtel on the Superbagnères balcony, a Tour finish several times; at the top the view of the Maladeta. Cleared all year.

sustenpass.note: Closure usually late October/November. Even gradient, Steingletscher panorama.

thyon-2000.note: From Sion via Vex and Les Collons up to the ski station above the Val d'Hérens, 1,550 m steadily steep. At the top the view across the Rhône valley to the Bernese Alps; open all year.

timmelsjoch.note: Toll road, scheduled to be open until mid/late October, then closed until June. Bikes ride toll-free.

tre-cime-di-lavaredo.classicAscent: 7.5 km, 7.6 % from Misurina, last 4 km at 12 %
tre-cime-di-lavaredo.note: Toll road, usually open until late October, then closed until May. Cars are charged, bikes ride free; when the car park is full the road is closed to cars, not to bikes.

triebener-tauern.note: The link from the Palten valley into the Pöls valley via Hohentauern; steep through a gorge from Trieben, flat from the south. Open all year.

turracher-hoehe.classicAscent: 9 km, 9.5 % from Ebene Reichenau, ramps of up to 23 %

ultental-weissbrunn.classicAscent: 15.9 km, 3.6 % from St. Walburg to Weißbrunn
ultental-weissbrunn.note: A dead-end valley behind Lana, past three reservoirs to the Weißbrunnsee beneath the Weißbrunnspitze. Little gradient, little traffic, old farmsteads and larches – the opposite of the Dolomite passes.

umbrailpass.note: Feeder to the Stelvio. Closure usually late October/November.

val-bavona.classicAscent: 16 km, 3 % from Cevio to San Carlo
val-bavona.note: The upper end of the Maggia valley: a road between granite walls and waterfalls, with no mains electricity and almost no cars, up to the cable car at San Carlo. Open all year, closed at times after heavy rain.

val-di-genova.note: The waterfall valley of the Adamello, from Carisolo to the Malga Bedole beneath the glaciers. In summer the upper part is closed to cars during the day (shuttle) – check the closure days beforehand; bikes may ride through at all times.

val-thorens.note: The highest ski resort in the Alps, cleared all year. Not a climb so much as an ascent: nearly 40 km in one go, never steep, never flat.

valgrisenche.classicAscent: 14.9 km, 5.8 % from Arvier to the head of the valley
valgrisenche.note: Past the Beauregard reservoir up to beneath the glaciers of the Grande Sassière – a dead end where almost nothing follows the lake. The old valley floor lies under the water, the road hangs above it on the flank.

valle-maira.note: The quietest of the Piedmontese valleys, with the rock tooth of the Provenzale above Chiappera at its end. Hardly any traffic, hardly any tourism – whoever rides the Maira rides it for the peace, not the gradient.

valle-verzasca.note: Over the dam James Bond jumped from, then along the emerald-green river to the head of the valley at Sonogno. Open all year; full of bathers at summer weekends, quiet in spring and autumn.

vallee-de-l-ubaye.note: The upper Ubaye valley ends at Maljasset beneath the three-thousanders. One of the quietest roads in the Western Alps; closed in winter.

vallee-de-la-claree.note: Dead-end valley full of larches and hamlets, the upper part closed to cars on summer days (shuttle from Névache – check the closure days beforehand). Little gradient, plenty of scenery.

vallee-des-chapieux.classicAscent: 19.1 km, 5.0 % from Bourg-Saint-Maurice to Ville des Glaciers
vallee-des-chapieux.note: Via Les Chapieux to the head of the valley beneath the Mont Blanc massif, where the road stops in front of the glacier. The last section is narrow and opens late in the year.

valmeinier-1800.classicAscent: 6.4 km, 6 % from the junction near Valloire
valmeinier-1800.note: A detour at the Télégraphe: from the Valloire basin the road climbs to the ski station of Valmeinier 1800.

valsavarenche.note: One of the three valleys of the Gran Paradiso, from Villeneuve in the Aosta valley to the head of the valley at Pont beneath the summit. National park throughout, little traffic, and at the end nothing but meadows and ibex.

valvestino.note: Up in hairpins from Gargnano on Lake Garda, then through tunnels and galleries high above the fjord of the Valvestino reservoir to the mountain village of Magasa. Open all year, almost no cars.

verbier.note: Short and steep from Le Châble in many hairpins up to the sunny terrace above the Val de Bagnes; a Tour de France finish in 2009. A ski resort with traffic, open all year.

villacher-alpenstrasse.note: Toll road, usually open until late October or longer. Bikes ride toll-free.

villard-reymond.classicAscent: 10.1 km, 7 % from the junction on the Ornon road
villard-reymond.note: A detour off the Ornon road: the narrow road climbs in hairpins to the mountain village of Villard-Reymond above the Oisans.

villnoesstal.classicAscent: 20.1 km, 5.6 % from Klausen to the Zanser Alm
villnoesstal.note: The valley beneath the Geisler peaks, ending at the Zanser Alm with the wall directly above it. Quiet, because it leads nowhere; the final kilometres from St. Magdalena climb noticeably.

vorderkaser-pfossental.classicAscent: 4.8 km, 10 % from the junction for the Pfossental
vorderkaser-pfossental.note: A detour in the Schnals valley: the road into the Pfossental climbs steeply to the Vorderkaser inn.

vrsic.classicAscent: 12 km, 8 % from Kranjska Gora, cobbled hairpins
vrsic.note: Julian Alps, 50 cobbled hairpins. Closure usually from November.

vue-des-alpes.note: The pass between Neuchâtel and La Chaux-de-Fonds, at the top in clear weather the whole Alpine chain from the Säntis to Mont Blanc. A main road with traffic, cleared all year.

wallbergstrasse.note: Mountain road closed to cars from Rottach-Egern to the Wallberghaus, a toboggan run in winter. Steadily steep in hairpins, at the top the view over the Tegernsee.

weinebene.note: The high crossing of the Koralpe between western Styria and the Lavant valley, 1,300 m of climbing from either side. Long, steady and quiet; open all year.

weissenstein.note: Solothurn's steep home climb: from Oberdorf more than 700 m in a short distance with ramps over 15 %, at the top the Alpine view from the Kurhaus. Closed in winter.

wildhaus.note: The crossing from the Rhine valley into the Toggenburg between the Churfirsten and the Alpstein, steep in hairpins from Gams, gentle from the Toggenburg. Open all year.

windische-hoehe.classicAscent: 12.8 km, 4.3 % from Feistritz an der Gail
windische-hoehe.note: A quiet crossing between the Gail and Drau valleys west of Villach, moderate on both sides. Open all year.

wolfgangpass.note: The main road from Klosters to Davos, short and steady from Klosters, barely any gradient from Davos – hence only one side. Open all year.

wurzenpass.note: Short, brutal and with lorry traffic: the northern ramp hits 18 % on the final kilometre. Border crossing into Slovenia, open all year – the reputation comes from the gradient, not the scenery.

zillertaler-hoehenstrasse.note: Toll road above the Zillertal from Ried to over 2,000 m at the Melchboden, almost 1,500 m of climbing with long double-digit ramps. At the top the panorama of the Zillertal Alps; closed in winter.

zinal.note: The Val d'Anniviers to its end, below the Imperial Crown of the Weisshorn, the Zinalrothorn, the Obergabelhorn, the Matterhorn and the Dent Blanche. Long and steady, open all year.

fichtelberg.note: Saxony's highest mountain: the road ends at the Fichtelberghaus just below the summit (1215 m). Short, around 9 % in the middle; a ski area in winter, the access road to the house is cleared.

klinovec.note: The highest mountain of the Ore Mountains, on the Bohemian side opposite the Fichtelberg. From Jáchymov the long climb through the forest, from Loučná the shorter one; at the top a lookout tower and a ski area.

komari-vizka.note: Steeply out of Krupka in hairpins up to the edge of the Ore Mountains, close to 9 % on average. At the top the Komáří vížka viewpoint above the North Bohemian Basin; the road carries on across the plateau to Fojtovice and Cínovec.

cinovec.note: The old border road from Teplice to Zinnwald, much quieter since the D8 motorway: steadily up through the forest onto the plateau, and on to Altenberg at the top.

medenec.note: Steadily out of the Ohře valley at Klášterec up to Měděnec below the Mědník hill, with a view back over the valley. At the top the road carries on across the plateau to Vejprty or Kovářská.

dlouha-louka.note: From Osek and its Cistercian monastery steeply up through the forest in hairpins onto the ridge at Dlouhá Louka; on to Moldava or Nové Město at the top.

auersberg.note: A dead-end road in the western Ore Mountains up the Auersberg, with a lookout tower and a mountain inn. Short from Wildenthal, long and gentle from Eibenstock; almost entirely in the forest.

bournak.note: A short dead-end road up the Bouřňák with its ski area and mountain hut, between Mikulov and Moldava on the ridge. At the top a view south over the basin.

schauinsland.note: Freiburg's own mountain: from Günterstal up the old hill-climb course in countless bends to over 1200 m, then on across Hofsgrund to the Notschrei. Many motorbikes at weekends.

kandel.note: From Waldkirch in the Elz valley up more than 900 metres to the Kandel, one of the hardest climbs of the Black Forest. From St. Peter on the other side it is only a short counter-climb, hence the one ascent here.

feldbergpass.note: The highest road crossing of the Black Forest, below the Feldberg (1493 m) between the Wiese valley and the Titisee. A main road with heavy traffic, a ski area in winter, and cleared.

notschrei.note: Crossing from the Dreisam valley into the Wiese valley between the Schauinsland and the Feldberg, with the cross-country ski centre at the pass. From Oberried the longer and finer side, from Todtnau the shorter one.

wiedener-eck.note: Up the long Münster valley to the saddle between the Belchen and the Schauinsland, with a wide view of the Belchen at the top. From Wieden on the east side it is barely 200 metres of climbing, hence one ascent.

hochblauen.note: A dead-end road from Badenweiler up the Blauen, the south-westernmost thousand-metre peak of the Black Forest: steep, without a flat stretch, and at the top a lookout tower with a view over the Rhine plain and, on a föhn day, to the Alps.

kniebis.note: Crossing from the Rench valley to Freudenstadt at the Alexanderschanze: from Oppenau on the country road up the Lierbach valley and in hairpins, then flat across the top. To the east the road barely drops, hence one ascent.

ruhestein.note: From Seebach in the Acher valley up to the Black Forest High Road at the national park; the B500 crosses at the top. Towards Baiersbronn the road drops long and gently through the Obertal, hence one ascent.

sa-calobra.note: Mallorca's most famous road: from the cove of Sa Calobra up dozens of hairpins and under the knotted tie (Nus de sa Corbata) to the Coll dels Reis. First down, then back – the other side from the junction on the Ma-10 is only a short counter-climb. Coaches during the day, free early in the morning.

puig-major.note: The island's highest road point, on the Ma-10 below the summit of the Puig Major (itself a military zone). From Sóller long and steady with views of the sea, at the top a short tunnel and the Cúber and Gorg Blau reservoirs.

coll-de-soller.note: The old pass road between Palma and Sóller, almost free of cars since the tunnel: a ribbon of hairpins on both sides, longer and finer from Sóller.

coll-de-sa-batalla.note: From Caimari at the edge of the plain steadily up into the mountains towards Lluc, the most ridden climb on the island. At the top the petrol station on the col with its café, then on to Lluc and the Puig Major.

coll-d-honor.note: A narrow mountain road from Bunyola over the Coll d'Honor into the high valley of Orient, almost free of traffic. Towards Orient it drops only briefly, hence one ascent.

coll-de-femenia.classicAscent: 8.0 km, 5.3 % from the head of the valley above Pollença
coll-de-femenia.note: From Pollença on the Ma-10 into the mountains towards Lluc: after six flat kilometres along the valley, in hairpins up to the Coll de Femenia with a view back to the bay. At the top the road carries on across the high ground to Lluc.

puig-de-randa.note: The monastery mountain in the middle of the plain, with three sanctuaries one above the other and the Santuari de Cura at the top. Short and steady; the hill to ride from Palma when the Tramuntana is in the rain.

sant-salvador.note: A dead-end road from Felanitx to the Sant Salvador monastery in the south-east of the island, with the great cross and the view over the coast at the top. A goal for the days when the north is in the wind.

pas-de-peyrol.note: The highest road pass of the Massif Central, right below the summit of the Puy Mary, with three ascents out of three green valleys. A Tour de France stage finish in 2020. Closed in winter.

col-de-neronne.note: Crossing from Salers into the Le Falgoux valley, the western approach to the Pas de Peyrol. From Le Falgoux short and steep, from Salers long and gentle across the high pastures.

col-de-prat-de-bouc.note: Dead-end road from Murat via Albepierre onto the plateau below the Plomb du Cantal, with a small ski area and footpaths at the top. Steady and quiet.

col-de-la-croix-saint-robert.note: The crossing from Le Mont-Dore to Besse across the flank of the Puy de Sancy. From Le Mont-Dore the steep, fine side; towards Besse long and flat across the plateau. Closed in winter.

col-de-la-croix-morand.note: The crossing between Le Mont-Dore and the Lac Chambon on the D996, ridden several times by the Tour de France. From Chambon the longer side, with a view of the lake.

super-besse.note: The climb from Besse into the ski resort below the Sancy, a Tour de France stage finish in 1978, 1996, 2008 and 2011. The road ends in the resort; with the Croix Saint-Robert it makes a loop.

col-du-beal.note: The highest crossing of the Monts du Forez, between the Auvergne and the Loire, over the treeless jasseries. From the west the steeper side, from Chalmazel shorter. Closed in winter.

mont-aigoual.note: The summit with the weather station, reached from Valleraugue by almost 1200 metres of climbing in one go; a Tour de France stage finish in 2020. From Meyrueis longer and gentler across the causse. Often windy and misty at the top.

col-de-finiels.note: The crossing of the Mont Lozère, on the route Stevenson walked with his donkey. From Le Pont-de-Montvert the longer and steeper side, from Le Bleymard via the Mont Lozère ski station.

col-du-minier.note: From Le Vigan more than 1000 metres up through the forest to the ridge of the Aigoual; often the way to the summit from the south. Quiet, steady and shady.

brocken.note: The Brocken road from Schierke to the highest mountain in northern Germany is closed to cars and open to bikes; at the top the Brocken railway station, a weather station and many walkers. Often wind, fog and snow into May.

torfhaus.note: The B4 from Bad Harzburg onto the plateau of the Upper Harz, with the Brocken opposite. Steady, but a main road with a lot of traffic and motorbikes; quieter from Altenau.

hexentanzplatz.note: The steep hairpin road from Thale onto the plateau above the Bode gorge, with a cable car, a zoo and an open-air theatre at the top. Plenty of day-trip traffic at weekends.

rosstrappe.note: The Hexentanzplatz's sister on the other side of the Bode gorge: from Thale short and steep to the rock above the gorge; the road ends at an inn.

ravensberg.note: The dead-end road from Bad Sachsa to the viewpoint mountain on the southern edge of the Harz, with an inn at the top and a view across the southern foothills. Quiet, with steep ramps in the forest.

grosser-inselsberg.note: The most striking summit of the Thuringian Forest, on the Rennsteig. From Tabarz long and steep at the end, from Brotterode short and steep; inns and a wide view north at the top.

oberhof.note: The crossing of the Rennsteig at the winter sports resort of Oberhof, steadily through the forest from Zella-Mehlis. A wide road; to the north it falls long and gently to Tambach-Dietharz.

wasserkuppe.note: The highest mountain of the Rhön and of Hesse, the cradle of gliding: an airfield, a radar dome and day-trip crowds at the top. From Gersfeld long and steady, from Poppenhausen a little steeper.

kreuzberg-rhoen.note: The holy mountain of Franconia: from Bischofsheim steeply up to the monastery and its brewery below the summit. The road ends at the car park.

hochrhoenstrasse.note: From Fladungen up onto the Hochrhön road at the Black Moor, which then runs across the bare Long Rhön to Bischofsheim. A climb in the strict sense: flat and open at the top.

bretterschachten.note: The highest road point of the Bavarian Forest, between Bodenmais and Bayerisch Eisenstein below the Arber. From Bodenmais steadily steep in the forest; to the east long and gentler via Arberhütte.

brennes.note: The crossing at the Großer Arber between Bayerisch Eisenstein and Lohberg, at the valley station of the Arber cable car. From Eisenstein short and steep, towards Lohberg long past the Großer Arbersee.

dreisessel.note: The road up the border mountain where Bavaria, Bohemia and Austria meet, with a mountain inn and granite crags at the top and views across the Bohemian Forest and, with föhn, to the Alps.

klet.note: The local mountain of Český Krumlov and České Budějovice, with an observatory and the oldest stone lookout tower in Bohemia. The last kilometres are closed to cars and belong to cyclists.

churanov.note: From Stachy up onto the plateau of the Bohemian Forest at Zadov, with a weather station and a small ski area. At the top the road runs on flat to the raised bogs around Kvilda.

col-de-bavella.note: The pass below the Aiguilles de Bavella, the red granite needles in the south of the island. From Zonza short and steady, from Solenzara on the east coast thirty kilometres through the gorge of the Solenzara.

col-de-vergio.note: The highest road pass in Corsica, between the Forêt d'Aïtone and the Niolo. From Evisa uphill through tall Laricio pines; to the east long and gentle via Calacuccia.

col-de-vizzavona.note: The pass of the main road between Ajaccio and Bastia, which the 2013 Tour de France crossed on Corsica. Beech and pine forest, but a lot of traffic: better early in the morning or out of season.

col-de-sorba.note: The quiet link from Vivario to Ghisoni, steep and in hairpins on both sides. At the top the view across the ridge to Monte Rotondo.

col-de-verde.note: The long forest pass between Ghisoni and the Taravo valley, through one of the island's largest forests. Long and moderately steep on both sides, with flat stretches.

col-de-teghime.note: Bastia's local climb, over the ridge at the root of Cap Corse to Saint-Florent. At the top the view of both seas, the Tyrrhenian and the Gulf of Saint-Florent.

ospedale.note: From Porto-Vecchio onto the Ospedale plateau, with a reservoir, pine forest and a view over the bay. At the top the road carries on through the forest to Zonza and the Col de Bavella.

col-de-sevi.note: The pass between Vico and Evisa above the Gulf of Sagone, with views to the sea and the Cinto mountains. A day from Evisa together with the Vergio.

el-portillo.classicAscent: 30.1 km, 6.7 % from Puerto de la Cruz
el-portillo.note: The classic Teide climb: from the north coast through the Orotava valley and the pine forest to the rim of the Cañadas, 2,000 metres in one go. The pros' training ground in winter.

boca-de-tauce.note: The western gate to the Cañadas, where the roads from Chío and Vilaflor enter the crater. From the west coast a long, steady climb across lava fields and through pine forest.

izana.note: The ridge road along the island's spine, from La Esperanza through the pine forest to the Izaña observatory, the highest road point on Tenerife. The sea on both sides.

degollada-de-cherfe.note: The pass above the Masca gorge, between Santiago del Teide and the mountain village of Masca. From Masca four kilometres at over 11 % in tight hairpins, one of the steepest ramps in the Canaries.

cruz-de-tejeda.classicAscent: 12.7 km, 5.5 % from Vega de San Mateo
cruz-de-tejeda.note: The pass in the middle of Gran Canaria, on the rim of the Tejeda caldera with a view of the Roque Nublo and as far as the Teide. Short and steep from Tejeda, longer from San Mateo.

pico-de-las-nieves.classicAscent: 14.9 km, 7.3 % from Vega de San Mateo
pico-de-las-nieves.note: The road to the highest point you can ride on Gran Canaria, just under 1,950 m, with a view over the whole island and to the Teide on a clear day. Steep from San Mateo, long from San Bartolomé.

fataga.note: The home climb of the southern resorts: from Maspalomas through the Fataga gorge up to San Bartolomé de Tirajana. Long and steady, with palm oases and red rock walls.

roque-de-los-muchachos.classicAscent: 43.5 km, 5.4 % from Santa Cruz de La Palma
roque-de-los-muchachos.note: From the sea to 2,400 m: the longest continuous climb in Europe, from Santa Cruz de La Palma to the telescopes on the rim of the Caldera de Taburiente. Shorter and steeper from Garafía in the north.

angliru.note: The most feared climb of the Vuelta, a summit finish several times since 1999: over 13 % on average for the last six kilometres, the Cueña les Cabres at over 20 %. Mountain pastures and a view across Asturias at the top.

lagos-de-covadonga.note: The Vuelta's most famous summit finish, ridden more than twenty times since 1983: from Covadonga and its basilica up to the mountain lakes Enol and Ercina in the Picos de Europa. Partly closed to cars in summer.

puerto-de-san-lorenzo.note: The pass between Teverga and Somiedo, often in the Vuelta: from La Plaza in Teverga steadily steep across mountain pastures. On the west side down to Somiedo and the Farrapona.

alto-de-la-farrapona.note: The road through the Somiedo natural park to the border with León, a Vuelta finish several times. Long and irregular, lakes and limestone peaks at the top, bears in the forests.

puerto-de-pajares.note: The old main pass between Asturias and León, quieter since the motorway. From Pola de Lena long through the valley and then in hairpins up to the border; the Meseta on the south side.

alto-de-la-cobertoria.note: The steep pass between Lena and Quirós, often the curtain-raiser for the Angliru in the Vuelta. From Pola de Lena ten kilometres almost without a break at over 8 %.

puerto-de-san-glorio.note: The highest road pass in Cantabria, from Potes up the Liébana valley to the border with León. At the top the view of the Picos de Europa, the bear monument at the Mirador de Llesba.

pena-cabarga.note: The viewpoint above the bay of Santander, a Vuelta finish several times: short, with ramps over 15 % in the last kilometres, the monument and the view over the bay and the Cantabrian Mountains at the top.

hoya-de-la-mora.classicAscent: 29.1 km, 6.0 % from Cenes de la Vega
hoya-de-la-mora.note: Spain's highest paved road, from Granada past the Pradollano ski resort to the Hoya de la Mora at almost 2,500 m; a Vuelta finish several times. Above it the closed road carries on to the Veleta.

alto-del-purche.note: The little brother of the Sierra Nevada road, from Monachil across the slopes east of Granada. Quiet, with ramps over 10 % and a view of the city and the Alhambra.

collado-de-las-sabinas.note: The climb via Hazallanas, a Vuelta stage in 2017: from Güéjar Sierra on a narrow road with ramps over 13 % onto the ridge above the ski resort. One of the hardest climbs in Andalusia.

puerto-de-la-ragua.note: The highest year-round road pass in Andalusia, across the Sierra Nevada between the Alpujarra and the Marquesado. Steady at around 6 % on both sides, pine forest and cross-country trails at the top.

calar-alto.note: The road to the observatory on the highest point of the Sierra de los Filabres, a Vuelta finish several times. Long, bare and dry, the telescope domes at the top and a view over the Tabernas desert.

alto-de-velefique.note: The hairpin road out of the village of Velefique onto the Filabres ridge, a Vuelta pass and one of the finest hairpin ribbons in Spain. Steadily steep, with no traffic at all.

blockhaus.note: The Giro classic in the Majella, a summit finish again and again since Merckx's first Grand Tour stage win in 1967: almost 1,500 metres from Roccamorice with long stretches over 9 %, bare limestone slopes at the top.

passo-lanciano.note: The pass on the northern slope of the Majella, from Pretoro through beech forest; at the top the road to the Blockhaus begins. Often part of the Giro stages into the Abruzzo.

campo-imperatore.note: The road across the high plain below the Gran Sasso, Italy's little Tibet, to the hotel at 2,130 m; a Giro finish in 1971, 1989 and 2018. Long and open, the steep final ramp at the top.

terminillo.note: Rome's local mountain, from Rieti through chestnut and beech forest to the ski village of Pian de' Valli; a finish in Tirreno–Adriatico and the Giro. Steady and long.

passo-dell-abetone.note: The classic Apennine pass between Tuscany and Emilia, often in the Giro: from Cutigliano steadily through fir forest to the ski resort of Abetone.

san-pellegrino-in-alpe.note: The highest inhabited pass in the Apennines, from Castiglione in the Garfagnana; on the Chiozza side ramps of almost 20 %, one of the hardest places in Italy. Giro 1989 and 2022.

monte-amiata.note: The extinct volcano in southern Tuscany, with beech and chestnut forest almost to the summit. Steadily steep from Abbadia San Salvatore; at the top the view over the Crete and the Val d'Orcia.

sassotetto.note: The climb into the Monti Sibillini above Sarnano, a summit finish in Tirreno–Adriatico. Steadily steep through forest, the open meadows below the Sibillini ridge at the top.

etna-sud.note: The road up Etna to the Rifugio Sapienza at just over 1,900 m, a Giro finish several times. Three ascents from Nicolosi, Zafferana and Ragalna, black lava, craters and the cable car to the summit at the top.

etna-nord.note: Etna's north side, from Linguaglossa through pine and birch forest to the Piano Provenzana ski area at 1,800 m; a Giro finish in 2020. Quieter and greener than the south side.

piano-battaglia.note: The high plain of the Madonie at just over 1,600 m, Sicily's little ski area. From Isnello via Piano Zucchi through beech and holm oak, on across the plateau to Petralia.

portella-femmina-morta.note: The highest pass in the Nebrodi, on the road from the north coast via San Fratello to Cesarò. Through Sicily's great beech forests, almost without traffic.

portella-mandrazzi.note: The pass across the Peloritani between the north coast and the Alcantara valley. From Novara di Sicilia below the rocks of the Rocca Salvatesta, a view of Etna at the top.

erice.note: The medieval hill village at 750 m right above Trapani. Up the rock face from the coast in hairpins, a view over the salt pans to the Aegadian Islands at the top.

mur-de-huy.note: The finishing ramp of the Flèche Wallonne, from the Meuse in Huy up the Chemin des Chapelles to the chapel of Notre-Dame de la Sarte. Short, but with bends over 20 %.

cote-de-la-redoute.note: The best-known climb of Liège–Bastogne–Liège, steeply up from Remouchamps past the motorway; the fans' names painted on the tarmac.

cote-de-stockeu.note: The steepest ramp of Liège–Bastogne–Liège, out of the Amblève valley near Stavelot through the forest; the monument to Eddy Merckx at the top.

col-de-la-haute-levee.note: The climb north from Stavelot towards Francorchamps, a fixture of Liège–Bastogne–Liège. Steady, with the steepest stretch at the start.

col-du-rosier.note: The highest and longest climb in the finale of Liège–Bastogne–Liège, out of the Amblève valley through the forests above Spa.

cote-de-wanne.note: The climb from Trois-Ponts up to the village of Wanne, in Liège–Bastogne–Liège the first of the three blows Wanne, Stockeu and Haute-Levée.

cote-de-la-roche-aux-faucons.note: The ramp above the Ourthe valley near Esneux, often where the decisive attack comes in Liège–Bastogne–Liège. The rock at the top with the view over the bend of the Ourthe.

spindlerova-bouda.note: The mountain hut on the ridge at the Polish border, the highest road point in the Giant Mountains. From Špindlerův Mlýn through spruce forest with hairpins; on into Poland only on foot or by bike on the closed road.

przelecz-okraj.note: The border pass between Kowary in Silesia and Malá Úpa in Bohemia, Pomezní Boudy in Czech. Long from Kowary through the forest, with flatter stretches; huts at the top and the view to the Sněžka.

horni-misecky.note: The mountain village at the end of the road above Vítkovice, the start of the trails to the source of the Elbe. Short and steadily steep through spruce forest.

cerna-hora.note: The mountain road from the spa town of Janské Lázně to the Černá bouda below the summit of the Černá hora, closed to cars and signposted as a bike route. Hairpins in the forest at the bottom, ramps of up to 14 % at the top.

jested.note: The road up Liberec's home mountain to the TV tower with its hotel at just over 1,000 m, one of Czechia's landmarks. Steep and steady through the forest, over the open dome at the top.

tanvaldsky-spicak.note: The ski hill above Tanvald in the Jizera Mountains, with a steep road up to the lookout tower. Short, with ramps over 12 %.

strbske-pleso.note: The mountain lake and resort below the peaks of the High Tatras at just over 1,300 m. Long and steady from Štrba via Tatranská Štrba, the walls of the Tatras always in front of you.

certovica.note: The pass across the Low Tatras between Liptov and the Hron valley. Long and steady from the south, short and steeper from Vyšná Boca in the north.

chopok-juh.note: The southern ascent towards the Chopok, from Bystrá in the Hron valley past the Tále ski area to Srdiečko at just over 1,200 m. Steady, with steeper stretches in the upper part.

jasna.note: The northern ascent towards the Chopok, through the Demänovská valley past the entrance of the Freedom Cave to the Jasná ski area. The steep finish after the caves.

gliczarow-gorny.note: The ramp above Biały Dunajec near Zakopane, one of the steepest roads in Poland with stretches over 20 %. The view over the Podhale to the whole chain of the High Tatras at the top.

wierch-poroniec.note: The Oswald Balzer road from Zakopane through the forest of the Tatra National Park to the border at Łysa Polana. Long and rolling from Zakopane; from Łysa Polana only a short counter-climb of 3 km, hence one-sided.

pod-prislopom.note: The saddle above Ždiar between the Belianske Tatry and the Spišská Magura, on the road from Poprad to the Łysa Polana border crossing. Flat and steady from both sides, with a view of the limestone walls of the Belianske Tatry.

huty.note: The crossing in front of the Western Tatras between Liptov and Orava, on the road from Liptovský Mikuláš to Zuberec. From the south the longer and steeper climb through the village of Huty; to the north shorter and gentler, down into the valley below the Roháče.

vernarske-sedlo.note: The saddle at the eastern end of the Low Tatras on the main road from Poprad to the Hron valley, below the Kráľova hoľa. Short and steady from Vernár, from Telgárt over the lower saddle of Besník.

baerenstein.note: A short, steep dead-end road from the village of Bärenstein up the basalt hill on the border, with a mountain inn and a lookout tower at the top; a stamp point of the Stoneman Miriquidi Road.

drei-brueder-hoehe.note: From the Preßnitz valley at Boden steadily up to the height between Wolkenstein and Marienberg with its lookout tower; at the top the road carries on across the plateau to Marienberg.

schwartenberg.note: From Olbernhau through the toy-making village of Seiffen up to the inn below the summit of the Schwartenberg, with a wide view over the eastern Ore Mountains; at the top the road carries on to Neuhausen.

nova-ves-v-horach.note: From Litvínov-Janov up the escarpment of the Ore Mountains, with views back over the North Bohemian Basin; at the top the road carries on across the plateau to Brandov or Hora Svaté Kateřiny.

col-d-osquich.note: The low crossing from the Pays de Cize into the Soule, a stage of the Raid Pyrénéen and several times of the Tour de France. Green Basque hills, open all year.

col-des-ares.note: The forest pass between the Garonne valley and the valley of the Ger, the way from the Luchonnais to the Portet d'Aspet on the Raid Pyrénéen and in the Tour de France. Open all year.

col-de-la-perche.note: The gentle high pass between the Cerdagne and the Capcir near Mont-Louis, on the Raid Pyrénéen the last roof before the descent to the Mediterranean. A main road, cleared all year.

coll-de-sa-gramola.note: The crossing of the Ma-10 coast road from Estellencs to Andratx, on the Mallorca 312 and many loops in the island's south-west. Open all year.

galilea.note: The climb to the mountain village of Galilea above the south-west, on the Mallorca 312 and a classic of the loops from Calvià. Narrow, little traffic, on over the Coll des Grau to Puigpunyent.

col-du-menil.note: The low crossing from the Moselle valley at Le Thillot over into the valley of the Moselotte, on the Grand Tour des Ballons the way to Cornimont. Open all year.
